Sports.title: Bradley Barcola due for medical as Liverpool finalise £123m deal for winger
Sports.content:
Liverpool have finalised a deal worth up to £123m for Bradley Barcola, with the Paris Saint-Germain winger to undergo a medical this weekend for his move to Anfield.

Liverpool agreed the outline of a deal with the Champions League holders on Wednesday night, after lengthy talks over their main summer transfer target.

The structure of the package has now been accepted and the Anfield club will pay £106m up front for the 23-year-old, plus £17m in add-ons based on individual and team achievements.

Personal terms with Barcola have already been agreed, with the France international’s representatives giving the green light to his transfer to Merseyside last month.

The winger is set to have a medical over the weekend before completing a transfer that will make him the second-most expensive signing in Liverpool’s history, behind Alexander Isak.

Liverpool’s other incoming senior players so far this summer are the centre-back Ronald Araújo, on loan from Barcelona, the Osasuna winger Víctor Muñoz and the defender Jérémy Jacquet, whose £55m move from Rennes was agreed in January.

Sports.title: Alonso gets Chelsea’s priorities right by ditching Sánchez for winner Martínez | Jacob Steinberg
Sports.content:
Carlo Cudicini was a very good goalkeeper. However, José Mourinho was ruthless when he became Chelsea manager in 2004. Very good was not good enough. Mourinho wanted the best and one of the main factors behind the Portuguese winning the Premier League during his first season in charge was the decision to replace Cudicini with Petr Cech.

There is an old line about a great goalkeeper being worth 15 points a season. It is not for nothing, for instance, that Brian Clough regarded Peter Shilton as one of his most important signings at Nottingham Forest. Shilton was key when Forest defied the odds by winning the Division One title in 1978 and there are plenty of other examples of promising teams taking the next step only after buying a top No 1.

Jürgen Klopp’s Liverpool did not become the finished article until signing Alisson in 2018, while Arsenal might not have finished top last season without David Raya’s crucial save during the 1-0 win over West Ham in May. Chelsea, though, developed a blind spot after selling Thibaut Courtois to Real Madrid eight years ago.

A host of inconsistent goalkeepers have come and gone, or in some cases stuck around long after it became clear they were not a patch on Cech and Courtois, and it is only now that Chelsea have tackled the issue head on.

The £7.5m signing of Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa adds to the sense that this will go down as the summer when BlueCo got serious. The focus on youth remains but has lowered in intensity and the decision to ditch Robert Sánchez after his clumsy performance during last Monday’s 3-2 win over Fulham shows that Xabi Alonso will not hesitate to make the big calls.

The only frustration for supporters is that it has taken this long for Chelsea to give up on Sánchez, three years after signing him from Brighton for £25m. There have been occasional challenges but none have lasted. Mauricio Pochettino switched to Djordje Petrovic midway through the 2023-24 season, only for Enzo Maresca to return to Sánchez after becoming Chelsea’s head coach in the summer of 2024.

Filip Jörgensen, signed from Villarreal as Sánchez’s deputy two years ago, then had chances to establish himself as the No 1. Jörgensen is better than Sánchez with his feet but struggled to convince. Maresca did not stick with the Dane after bringing him into the side in February 2025. The turning point in Liam Rosenior’s brief reign came when his decision to select Jörgensen over Sanchez in a Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain last season backfired so badly that Chelsea lost 5-2.

Jörgensen departed this summer and it seemed that Chelsea were going to ignore all the outsiders who insisted that Sánchez also had to go. The message was that Alonso was happy with his options in goal. Sánchez was going to remain as the No 1 and the academy graduate Teddy Sharman-Lowe was third choice, while part of the thinking behind the club’s refusal to go into the market for a new goalkeeper was their belief that Mike Penders is going to become one of the best in the world.

Penders, who made his debut in the Carabao Cup win over Luton on Thursday, joined from Genk for £17m two years ago. Chelsea’s determination not to block the 21-year-old Belgian’s pathway partly explains why they have not pursued opportunities to sign Milan’s Mike Maignan and Porto’s Diogo Costa during the past two summers.

This was supposed to be a season of gradual change. Sánchez was still first pick but was going to face healthy competition from Penders. Both were content with that situation. Ben Roberts, Chelsea’s head of goalkeeping, worked with Sánchez at Brighton and has long been one of his biggest advocates.

Yet Sánchez’s performance against Fulham forced Chelsea’s hand. It was clear that there was not going to be a title challenge unless a new goalkeeper was signed before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. The proof was overwhelming. Sánchez dribbled the ball behind for a corner at one point and was at fault for both Fulham goals. He spread anxiety, making his defenders nervous, and Alonso knew it was time to act.

Things moved quickly when Chelsea were contacted by Martínez’s representatives earlier this week. The club’s sporting leadership presented the idea to Alonso, who gave them the green light, and the transfer was completed on Thursday night.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea believe 21-year-old Mike Penders can become one of the best goalkeepers in the world. Photograph: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

There was some doubt about whether it would be a permanent deal. Some people wondered if a loan would make more sense, ensuring this was a temporary fix rather than one to spook Penders.

More pressingly, meanwhile, there were warnings about Sánchez’s mood. There was concern over whether the 28-year-old would accept an immediate demotion. Yet Chelsea have not worried about hurt feelings. There is little time to act but Sánchez needs to leave. He will be frozen out if he stays and looks unlikely to feature when Chelsea host Brighton on Sunday. There is interest from clubs in England, Europe and Saudi Arabia.

This is life at the top. Chelsea have been decisive. Sánchez is capable of wondrous saves, can command his area and is liked in the dressing room, but he is shaky with his feet and prone to calamitous games. Chelsea needed stability. They watched Pochettino, Maresca and Rosenior change goalkeeper during the season. It is better to have a clear hierarchy from the start.

Enter Martínez, who has long been looking for a way out of Villa. He almost joined Manchester United last summer and recently appeared to be on his way to Juventus. Villa have moved on, signing Zion Suzuki. Martínez has been a great servant but wanted a new challenge. Chelsea assessed the conditions of a deal. Martínez had other offers but wanted to play for Alonso. That desire convinced Chelsea to do the deal.

It makes sense. Martínez is 34 next week and has signed on a two-year deal, with the option of an extra year. Penders has an experienced mentor. He can continue to grow and knows his time will come.

Chelsea are focused on the present. Martinez has a winning mentality – he is Argentina’s No 1 and a World Cup winner in 2022 – and has been one of the best goalkeepers in England since joining Villa from Arsenal in 2020. There is still no guarantee Chelsea will challenge Arsenal’s dominance but they surely have a better chance with Martínez in goal.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 8: Everton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 10th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 8th

Prospects

With a new manager in charge, there is fresh optimism for Everton. But nobody associated with the club will be getting carried away. Last season concluded with a respectable eighth-place finish and anything similar again would be considered a solid campaign for a team operating on a relatively small budget. The latest set of accounts showed Everton’s wage bill to be five times smaller than Chelsea’s, illustrating the financial gulf between them and those challenging at the top of the Women’s Super League.

There have been positive elements to Everton’s transfer business this summer, not least the arrivals of Jutta Rantala, Noémie Mouchon and Hannah Cain from relegated Leicester, as well as turning the Slovenia midfielder Zara Kramzar’s loan move from Roma into a permanent deal. Last season’s loan move for Hannah Blundell from Manchester United has also been converted into a permanent transfer, which was revealed in unusual circumstances, with the 32-year-old emerging from a make-shift coffin during a walkout at May’s World Sevens Football event in London.

They have a fairly kind start to the season,beginning with back-to-back matches against promoted Crystal Palace and Charlton. Their second home league fixture is against the other promoted side, Birmingham. In between there are meetings with the sides that finished 10th and 11th last season, in West Ham and Liverpool. Everton do not face any of last season’s top three teams until November. They will, therefore, be keen to make a fast start and get plenty of points onboard before a tougher-looking run of games either side of the winter break.

Off-field picture

The women’s team was sold to the men’s parent company, Roundhouse Capital Holdings, last year in a move that was understood to be largely aimed at helping ensure the men’s team’s compliance with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules (PSR). They train at the Finch Farm complex in Halewood, which they share with the men. It is one of the better-equipped facilities enjoyed by a WSL side.

The manager

Scott Phelan was formally appointed in June after a four-month spell in interim charge, taking over from the sacked Brian Sørensen. This is the 38-year-old former Everton youth midfielder’s first senior managerial job, after coaching in the club’s boys’ academy. Phelan deploys a calm, measured approach and has spoken of his pride at being given this job.

Star signing

There is a lot of excitement at Everton about the Australia forward Holly McNamara, signed from Melbourne City, where she won back-to-back Golden Boot awards in the A-League, on a free transfer. If the 23-year-old can replicate her goalscoring form in the northern hemisphere, Everton could well have a strong season and, with McNamara alongside Cain and Mouchon, they have a completely new-look attack. The England youth centre-back Hannah Silcock has also been snapped up from Liverpool, which looks like an astute piece of business.

View image in fullscreen Holly McNamara won back-to-back Golden Boots during her time at Melbourne City and has been handed the No 9 shirt at Everton. Photograph: Patrick Snow Jr/Everton FC

Stat attack

Despite having the third-fewest shots last season, Everton had the third most from Opta-defined fast breaks (counterattacks). They also scored the joint-most goals from them (four), but that can only carry them so far. Their attack in regular play needs work.

Set for a breakthrough

The England youth defender Naomi Layzell has arrived on loan from Manchester City and Everton and the Lionesses will be hoping it can be a good year for the fit-again 22-year-old. Layzell came to prominence with a goal against Barcelona in the Women’s Champions League two years ago, but has since suffered injury misfortune. There is hope at Everton that Layzell can kick on this season and show why she is potentially a future regular for England. She has previously been called up to train with the senior side.

What they say

“It’s been a tough pre-season in terms of the physical load, but that’s great preparation for the season. It’s just so important to get everyone on the same page early on” – Everton goalkeeper Courtney Brosnan

Where are they playing their home games?

The women’s team moved to Goodison Park last summer and will continue to play all of their home games there. They made their debut at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last season in a one-off appearance, losing to Manchester United, and while there is no confirmation of when they will next play at the men’s ground, it is understood that is not off the table for the new campaign.

Sports.title: Who was given the toughest fixtures in the Champions League draw?
Sports.content:
The 36 clubs in the Champions League know who they will play in the league phase, but which team has the kindest draw and who has the toughest assignment? Each side knows their eight opponents, but, given no two teams face the same set of opponents, this is not a level playing field. We have used the Opta power rankings – which rank 16,000 teams from across the world on the same scale – to find out who did best in the draw.

Quick Guide Champions League 26/27 fixtures Show Who have the English clubs got? Arsenal: Napoli (a), 9 September; Lille (h), 13 October; Bayern Munich (a), 21 October; Slavia Prague (a), 4 November; Borussia Dortmund (h), 24 November; Real Madrid (h), 9 December; Real Betis (a), 20 January; Sabah (h), 27 January Aston Villa: Club Brugge (a), 8 September; Fenerbahçe (h), 14 October; Viking (h), 21 October; Barcelona (a), 3 November; Galatasaray (a), 24 November; PSG (h), 8 December; Borussia Dortmund (h), 19 January; Slavia Prague (a), 27 January Liverpool: Atlético Madrid (h), 9 September; LASK (a), 14 October; Villarreal (h), 20 October; Fenerbahçe (a), 4 November; Club Brugge (a), 25 November; Porto (h), 9 December; Inter Milan (a), 19 January; Lens (h), 27 January Manchester City: Porto (a), 8 September; PSG (h), 14 October; AEK Athens (h), 20 October; RB Leipzig (a), 4 November; Napoli (h), 24 November; Barcelona (a), 8 December; Lens (a), 20 January; Sporting CP (h), 27 January Manchester United: Sabah (h), 10 September; Atlético Madrid (a), 13 October; Como (a), 21 October; Roma (h), 3 November; Sporting CP (a), 25 November; RB Leipzig (h), 8 December; Bayern Munich (h), 20 January; Villarreal (a), 27 January Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Which teams have the easiest fixtures?

In terms of Premier League clubs, Liverpool have received the easiest draw. Their eight opponents have an average rating of 90.0, making theirs the ninth-kindest fixture list overall. Atlético Madrid and Inter were the two easiest pot-one opponents Premier League clubs could draw and Liverpool will play them both – starting with Atlétco at home. They visit San Siro to face Inter in January.

Arsenal also received a relatively favourable draw, albeit for different reasons. Their pot-one fixtures against Bayern Munich (away) and Real Madrid (home) are about as difficult as they come – and they also drew Dortmund, the highest-ranked team in pot two – but, beyond those games and an opening trip to Napoli, there is little for them to fear. Arsenal drew the two lowest-ranked sides in pot four: Sabah, who they host in their final group game, and Slovan Bratislava. While the top end of their draw is tough, the bottom end is kind.

View image in fullscreen The 18 easiest draws.

Stuttgart received the easiest draw, with their opponents having an average rating of 88.9. Inter came out of the draw particularly well, receiving the second-easiest set of fixtures, with an average opponent rating of 89.5. Having finished as runners-up in 2024-25, Inter suffered a surprise exit at the hands of Bodø/Glimt in the playoff stage last season. Given their relatively easy schedule, they will hope to avoid that stage and qualify directly for the last 16.

Which teams have the toughest fixtures?

Manchester City will begin a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola for the first time in 11 years. His replacement, Enzo Maresca, has been handed the most difficult fixture list of any Premier League club. City’s opponents have an average rating of 91.7, with only five teams receiving a tougher draw overall. They have drawn two European giants in pot one – Barcelona and PSG – while Napoli are a particularly difficult assignment from pot three. City begin at Porto and then host PSG in their second game; Napoli (at home) and Barça (away) are back-to-back November fixtures.

Aston Villa also drew Barcelona and PSG from pot one, although they have fond memories of their previous meeting with the European champions at Villa Park. Villa won the second leg of their quarter-finals 3-2 at home in April 2025, falling just short over the tie as they lost 5-4 on aggregate. Villa’s squad has changed significantly since then, however, and they were also given the toughest possible pair of opponents from pot two in Club Brugge, who they visit in their first game, and Dortmund.

Their opponents from the lower pots are more forgiving, but Unai Emery will need to work his European magic if a squad that has undergone significant churn this summer is to make another deep run in the competition. They at least have time to settle before hosting PSG and Dortmund in their final home games of the league phase.

View image in fullscreen The 18 toughest draws.

Manchester United are back in the Champions League for the first time since 2023-24. Their previous campaign did not go particularly well, losing four of their six games and finishing bottom of their group. Their draw this season is not disastrous, but it is definitely on the more difficult side.

They face Bayern Munich and Atlético Madrid from pot one and have drawn Como – the most difficult opponent in pot four. Fixtures against Sporting CP and Roma should also be highly competitive, while United drew RB Leipzig and Villarreal from pot three. They were not the worst possible outcomes, but there were certainly plenty of more favourable draws available. United open at home to Sabah, but then face trips to Atlético and Como before Roma travel to Old Trafford.

It is no surprise to see Sabah and Slavia Prague emerge with the hardest and third-hardest fixture lists, respectively. Beyond those two, Lens received a particularly difficult draw, with their opponents’ average rating at 92.1. Atlético Madrid were not far behind on 92.0.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: José Mourinho claims Real Madrid’s Mbappé should win Ballon d’Or this year
Sports.content:
José Mourinho has said Kylian Mbappé deserves to win this year’s Ballon d’Or, arguing the award should go to the best player in the world rather than be decided by World Cup or Champions League success.

“The best players in the world, there are two, three or four of them, and we know who they are: they’re here,” the Real Madrid coach said on Saturday before their game against Málaga in La Liga.

“For me, there is one who, individually, made history this summer,” Mourinho said, in reference to Mbappé, who became the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history.

View image in fullscreen ‘You cannot give the Ballon d’Or to a player simply because he won the Champions League or the World Cup,’ says José Mourinho. Photograph: Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

The France captain is among the contenders for the Ballon d’Or after finishing last season as the top scorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the 2026 World Cup, despite failing to win a major trophy. His rivals include the England striker Harry Kane, the Spain midfielder and World Cup winner Rodri and Paris Saint-Germain’s European champions Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Mbappé, who scored a hat-trick in Wednesday’s 4-1 win over Real Sociedad, featured on the front page of Madrid-based sports daily AS on Saturday under the headline: “Mbappé targets the Ballon d’Or”.

“You cannot give the Ballon d’Or to a player simply because he won the Champions League or the World Cup,” said Mourinho. “The Ballon d’Or should go to one of those players who, when they retire, will be missed for ever. Maradona, Ronaldinho, Ronaldo Nazario, Cristiano Ronaldo, Messi, Zidane …” he said.

“If we want to reward the Champions League, then give it to Luis Enrique. For the Spanish national team, give it to [Luis] De la Fuente. The best player in the world is something else and he is neither at PSG nor in the Spain team.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola fumes after his Liverpool substitutions are delayed when the fourth official's board breaks - then sees his side concede a penalty in draw to Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was left aggrieved by a fourth-official fumble that cost his team a goal as they could only manage another draw to start the season.

New signing Victor Munoz equalised after Nottingham Forest had twice led through Dan Ndoye and a Morgan Gibbs-White penalty, with Alexander Isak also opening his account for the campaign.

But Iraola thought the second Forest goal was unfair given he was unable to make a substitution for three minutes due to the fourth official’s electric board not working and, when the changes should have occurred, the away team took a quick throw-in that led to the penalty being awarded.

‘I will analyse the penalty, but this cannot be a professional fourth official,’ he said.

‘It cannot take… I don’t know, three minutes (for him to ready the board). We’ve already given the subs’ numbers two or three minutes before.

‘I was already angry because in the previous stoppage we couldn’t make (the triple sub), and before the throw-in I said, “OK we’ll do it now”. But I don’t know (what happened).

‘They will have to explain it, but it has taken ages to not prepare two boards.’

Liverpool's three substitutes are ready to enter the fray but the fourth official's board is down

Five seconds later Andoni Iraola looks across to see what is happening

It was quick thinking by Forest new boy Liam Delap but Iraola was frustrated that he should have been instead allowed to make his triple change after a lengthy delay. He would also argue that the changes might have helped his team defend the attack that led to the penalty.

Daily Mail Sport has approached the Premier League for comment over the fourth official incident.

Liverpool, meanwhile, will complete the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola in the next 24 hours. He is set to jet into England from Paris on Sunday ahead of a medical and five-year deal.

He could take the No29 shirt which he wears at Paris Saint-Germain after a character on the FIFA video game, Alex Hunter, who wore that number after rising up from park pitches to the top level.

Iraola said on Barcola, Liverpool’s third £100million-plus player: ‘I cannot tell you anything right now but it is true that there are things going on and that is normal.

More than a minute later the ball goes out but Forest take a quick throw-in...

... and with their substitutes still not on Liverpool concede a penalty and go 2-1 down

‘We are in the last weeks of the market and now we have to wait to see the squad that we will have on September 2, and this is who we are.’

Forest boss Oliver Glasner was delighted with his first point in charge and also discussed transfers, with his side on the verge of signing his former colleague Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace. They also want Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong and have discussed a £40million move for the 19-year-old.

Glasner was asked if it would be just those two arriving and said: ‘Could be more.

‘I have no idea. I have just played outside. I am full of emotions, very confident that we find the right players and characters and today everyone involved in the game deserves us to be talking about him. They deserve all the credit.

‘I will sleep when (the window) is closed and on Wednesday evening I will have a pint and celebrate the transfer window.’

Sports.title: Shocking moment shameless Liverpool fan snatches Alexander Isak's shirt from a child at Anfield
Sports.content:
A Liverpool fan has been savaged on social media after snatching Alexander Isak's shirt from a child following the Anfield club's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

Goalscorer Isak was making his way towards the tunnel when he spotted a young fan in the stands. The Swede removed his shirt before offering it to the supporter.

However, as he made the move to hand over the jersey, an older fan swiped the shirt from the youngster's grasp, taking Isak aback.

The thieving fan was then seen grinning widely as he made for a hasty exit.

However, onlookers lambasted the individual for the shameless act, and he was later seen giving the shirt to the intended recipient.

Grown ass man tried to snatch away a shirt given by Isak to a kid...Embarrassing pic.twitter.com/0dAPD8xOWo — The Culé 🇧🇪 (@TheBelgianCule) August 29, 2026

A Liverpool fan shamelessly snatched Alexander Isak's shirt from a young supporter

Liverpool striker Isak made a beeline for the youngster but the shirt was stolen away

Footage of the incident has gone viral online, with rival fans offering a scathing verdict.

'Don’t these morons realize there are cameras everywhere these days?' one user said on X.

'Grown man steaming a sweaty kit off a child… should be banned from entering Anfield again,' said another.

'Glad the kid got it back, infuriating that grown men act like this.'

Others credited the bystanders for intervening.

'Credit to the guys who called him out causing him to give it to the boy,' one fan said.

'Fair play to Isak for seeing that and making sure the scruff gave it back. How embarrassing…'

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola set for Liverpool medical in next 24 hours ahead of £123m move to Premier League club: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest agree £22m deal for Daniel Munoz, Leeds keen on Leipzig forward, Besiktas ask about Pape Matar Sarr, Spurs reject loan offer for centre back... and Liverpool agree deal for Bradley Barcola: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Munoz set for Forest in £22m deal

Daniel Munoz is set to complete a move to Nottingham Forest after the club agreed a deal in principle with Crystal Palace.

The Colombian international, a favourite of Oliver Glasner, is set to link up with his old boss at the City Ground for a fee of about £22million.

Munoz was a key player in the Glasner era at Selhurst Park, when the Eagles won three trophies. But at 30, Palace believe this is a good deal ahead of the transfer window closing on September 1.

Forest drew 2-2 at Liverpool today and are keen to strengthen in midfield, with talks underway to sign Harrison Armstrong from Everton for about £40m.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Forest are also prepared to let winger Omari Hutchinson depart after leaving him out of the squad at Anfield. AC Milan have shown a strong interest in the England Under-21 international and if talks proceed smoothly, he could fly to Italy as soon as Sunday.

Discussions between the clubs have centred around an initial season-long loan deal with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met. Milan are managed by former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim and have started the season with two wins.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Daniel Munoz is set to move to Nottingham Forest

Gunners snap up United winger

Arsenal have announced the signing of winger James Scanlon from Manchester United. The deal is a free transfer but United retain a 50 per cent sell-on.

The 19-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at League Two side Swindon Town, where he scored his first senior club goal and helped the Robins finish ninth. However, he was viewed as having little chance of making an impact on United’s first team.

Scanlon is already a Gibraltar international, earning 24 senior caps and featuring in World Cup qualifiers and Nations League matches.

'I can’t wait to get started,' Scanlon told the club’s official website. 'I’ve been waiting to get this over the line, so I’m buzzing to be here.'

Arsenal have also agreed a deal to sign 17-year-old Georgian attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili ahead of Paris Saint-Germain.

The teenager is due to have a medical next week before joining in the New Year.

James Scanlon already has plenty of international experience with Gibraltar

United academy star heads for Rotherham loan

Manchester United academy midfielder Jayce Fitzgerald is set to join Rotherham United on loan.

Daily Mail Sport understands the 19-year-old, who has never previously been out on loan, is keen to test himself in a senior set-up after excelling at Under-21s level.

Fitzgerald will head to Rotherham, the club who helped develop fellow Manchester United youngster Dan Gore last season. Gore won their Player of the Season award.

NATHAN SALT

Jayce Fitzgerald, here in Manchester United training, is taking his first steps in senior football

Foxes on the hunt

Leicester City, who visit MK Dons in League One today, want to sign either George Dobson or Matty James from Wrexham and are asking about both midfielders.

Wrexham are still in for Leicester centre back Harry Souttar as they juggle targets.

City's Bah talks over move to Germany

Manchester City centre back Juma Bah is in talks to join Augsburg on loan.

The 20-year-old 6ft 5in defender spent last season on loan at Nice.

Leeds try Harder ahead of deadline

Leeds United maintain an interest in RB Leipzig forward Conrad Harder though they face competition for the Denmark international.

Leipzig are finalising a deal for Chelsea's Marc Guiu to increase competition for places. Leeds winger Willy Gnonto is attracting attention from Fiorentina meanwhile.

The winger has missed Leeds' first two games of the season with a hamstring injury he sustained during pre-season.

Conrad Harder is subject of interest from several clubs, including Leeds

Black Cats enquire about Malick

Sunderland have asked about Lyon winger Malick Fofana.

The 21-year-old has been discussing a move to Roma but Sunderland have made a late check as their own pursuit of a winger has hit a few bumps.

They remain in talks for Igor Paixao from Marseille and had placed an offer for Geny Catamo at Sporting Lisbon but have still to reach breakthrough.

They also enquired for Manchester City's Jack Grealish earlier this week but believe he may end up at Tottenham.

Besiktas ask about Sarr

Besiktas have asked about signing Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr on a permanent deal.

The Senegal international also has Monaco and Nottingham Forest offers to consider

Elliott a target for Valencia

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott is being eyed by Spanish side Valencia.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, the 23-year-old has interest from a number of clubs with Lazio and Napoli among them but Valencia are hopeful they can sign the England U21 international on loan.

Liverpool have still to receive an official approach but are aware of interest.

Harvey Elliott was not part of Liverpool's squad for the clash with Nottingham Forest today

Malaga push for Everton's Aznou

Malaga are progressing in talks to sign Adam Aznou from Everton.

Aznou came on as a substitute in the 4-0 win over Preston North End in midweek but has struggled since joining from Bayern Munich.

Everton have checked on Melvin Bard at Nice, among others.

Toon press on with Pardo move

Newcastle United are continuing to discuss a move for Lille forward Mathias-Fernandez Pardo and appreciate Bilal El Khannouss at Stuttgart.

El Khannouss, formerly of Leicester, has been mentioned at Everton also as they anticipate bids for Iliman Ndiaye.

Fulham in for Vallecano defender

Fulham are trying to complete a deal for Rayo Vallecano defender Andrei Ratiu.

The Romania right-back has already approved the move but there had been interest from Nottingham Forest also. The 28-year-old can also play in midfield.

Everton have shown interest in Fulham's Timothy Castagne who has a year left in contract.

Forest in talks over £40m move for Everton teen

Nottingham Forest are continuing attempts to rebuild their midfield following Elliot Anderson’s sale.

They are speaking to Everton about a deal worth £40m for their homegrown 19-year-old midfielder Harrison Armstrong, who started against Crystal Palace last week.

They have enquired about a loan with option to buy Pape Matar Sarr from Tottenham, who also has Monaco interest.

And they are continuing talks with Corinthians for 20-year-old Brazilian Andre.

Forest are close to reaching an agreement with Crystal Palace for Daniel Munoz. Forest made a £22m bid earlier this week and negotiations are at the final stages.

Harrison Armstrong in Everton's opening game of the season against Crystal Palace

Mbaye due to undergo Villa medical

Ibrahim Mbaye is due to undergo his medical later today and complete his transfer to Aston Villa from Paris Saint-Germain over the weekend.

The contract is being finalised and the deal for the 18-year-old is worth £47m.

PSG are making up to £170m from the deals for Bradley Barcola and Mbaye.

Spurs reject loan offer for defender

Tottenham have rejected a loan offer from Sunderland for Kevin Danso.

Sunderland explored the potential of taking the 27-year-old on a season loan.

Tottenham paid £21m for the defender last year

Spurs have rejected a loan offer from Sunderland for centre back Kevin Danso

Barcola set for Liverpool medical

Bradley Barcola is due on Merseyside this weekend to undergo a medical after Liverpool and Paris Saint Germain reached agreement on a £106million fee rising to £123m.

The 23-year-old France international is set sign a Liverpool contract until 2031 after the Anfield club finalised the structure of the transfer over the past 24 hours.

Liverpool are now set to pay £17m in add-ons.

Documents are still to be exchanged between the clubs and details are being arranged for Barcola to travel.

Liverpool are continuing to pursue another winger though Crystal Palace want a substantial fee for Ismaila Sarr after initial conversations last week.

Alternatives are being explored though Sarr, 28, is keen on the move. Palace have also asked about Torino's Alieu Njie and are in the throes of selling Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: New Liverpool co-owner spotted at Anfield for first time since leading consortium in buying £1.65billion stake alongside Amazon's billionaire founder Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
Liverpool's new co-owner Amit Bhatia was spotted at Anfield for the first time since leading a consortium in buying a £1.65billion stake in the football club. Bhatia's 1892 Holdings this month purchased the minority share in Liverpool, alongside billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos as well as Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin. On Saturday, Bhatia - who became Vice Chairman of the club following the investment - was seen in the stands sporting a club tie ahead of Andoni Iraola's first competitive match at Anfield. Iraola's side drew 2-2 for the second consecutive weekend, after battling back twice against Nottingham Forest in a repeat of their dramatic clash with Newcastle at St James' Park. Bhatia, who was previously director and co-owner of Championship side QPR, was unable to hide his delight at joining the iconic football club. 'It feels incredible,' Bhatia told club media on Friday. 'It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. Liverpool's new co-owner was spotted at Anfield for the first time on Saturday afternoon Amit Bhatia has led a consortium involving Jeff Bezos in purchasing a £1.65billion stake 'We're talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we're talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour. 'I'm just the biggest admirer of everything that is associated with this football club, whether it's the history and the culture, the supporters, the journey of this club, the owners in FSG, the management team at Liverpool. There's just so much to admire, so much to frankly be in awe of. 'And so to have the opportunity at this point in time, to hopefully potentially -- I want to just be very clear, subject to all kinds of regulatory approvals that we're going through the process [of] now -- but the simple fact that we've been potentially welcomed in by FSG to be part of such an incredible football club, a historic football club, an iconic football club like Liverpool, frankly it's the stuff of dreams. And it is the greatest honour I think that anybody can have.' Bhatia is a British-Indian millionaire who worked as an investment banker. His father-in-law, Lakshmi Mittal, is an Indian steel magnate with an estimated net worth of more than £22billion. 'I think again it's very important to emphasise that we're going through a regulatory process. That regulatory process is under way and we have to be incredibly respectful of that process. 'So it's important to say that, number one. Number two, I think it's important to be very clear that this club remains under the ownership of FSG. FSG are the decision-makers and this is their ownership. They have invited us and we're very fortunate to be a partner as a minority alongside them. 'And so my involvement really, or our involvement really, would be in any capacity that FSG felt that we could be useful to them. So, subject to regulatory [approval], in any capacity that FSG wants us to be involved, in any way that they think that we can add value for the betterment of the football club, is how we will make ourselves available at all times. 'We come from different geographies, we come from different professions, and hopefully with that you bring different experiences and ideas, different thoughts. If we are called upon, if there's any area that we have this expertise in or that FSG would like to discuss with us, our thoughts or our involvement, we would absolutely be there. Bhatia was pictured alongside Liverpool owner John W Henry pitchside ahead of the match 'We believe that the potential for the football club is still vast ahead of us and we have had some discussions with FSG as to those thoughts. 'And hopefully if everything goes well, our association with the club will also be for a very, very long period of time. And so as and when we can see those opportunities and we feel that they're in the best interests of the football club, as an entire group we'll come together and try to support in the best way that we think we can. 'And so that's very exciting to think about, because as I said, the potential is enormous. And we're very excited to see what the future holds for us in that regard.'

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard cheekily tells Nottingham Forest star he is needed at Liverpool after being quizzed on his transfer future on live TV
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard cheekily tells Nottingham Forest star he is needed at Liverpool after being quizzed on his transfer future on live TV

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard told Neco Williams he is needed at Anfield after the Nottingham Forest star was quizzed on his future.

Former Reds academy star Williams, 25, won a penalty as Forest held Andoni Iraola's side to a 2-2 draw on Saturday afternoon, with the new Liverpool boss still searching for his first competitive win.

Williams has been a standout performer at full-back in the Premier League in the past two seasons and his strong displays have naturally seen interest mount in securing his services.

Daily Mail Sport reported earlier in the window that Williams features on a list of transfer targets for Manchester United, while Newcastle are also admirers of the Welshman.

And Gerrard told Williams on TNT Sport 'we need full-back cover here' as Lynsey Hipgrave grilled him on his future, with question marks hanging over the quality of current full backs Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez.

That comment triggered a polite laugh from the 25-year-old, who insisted his focus remains on Forest.

Steven Gerrard cheekily told Neco Williams he is needed at Anfield on Saturday afternoon

Williams has been a standout performer and has seen interest mount in his services

'Listen every day I'm focused on the badge I'm wearing right now and that's Forest and that's all I can do.

'Of course it's nice to see that teams are showing interest but at the end of the day I'm a Forest player and I am focused on what I'm doing here.'

Gerrard's impromptu comment comes after United legend Peter Schmeichel was emphatically shot down by Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle when he asked the Toon manager about Lewis Hall's future.

'I think it will be a stressful period for the sporting director, because we have some needs.

'But if we bring players in maybe there will also be some players who go out.'

Former Man United keeper Peter Schmeichel, who played 398 times for the club, then cheekily said: 'We are looking at your left back.'

That comment was in reference to Hall, with United having made enquiries for the defender this summer.

But to that, Jaissle said: 'No chance, no chance,' as he chuckled.

Sports.title: Clunky, disconnected Liverpool are levels below where they need to be, writes IAN LADYMAN after Reds salvaged a point against Nottingham Forest - and one defender looks like he will never make it at Anfield
Sports.content:
In the final minute of this game, with Liverpool’s need at its deepest, the Dutch midfielder Ryan Gravenberch sold the Nottingham Forest defence a lovely dummy to allow his team-mate Alexander Isak a run on goal. Unfortunately for Liverpool, Isak had bought the dummy, too, and the ball ran away to insignificance.

And that very much sums up this Liverpool team. Clunky, disconnected and, as a result, largely starved of attacking menace. So far this season, Andoni Iraola’s team have survived on moments. Four times in two games they have trailed, against Newcastle and Forest, and four times they have recovered to take two draws which have served to keep the discontent to a mere grumble in the early days of Iraola’s reign.

There are some chinks of light. Isak – with so much resting on his shoulders this season – scored a goal and so, wonderfully, did summer signing, 23-year-old Spaniard Victor Munoz. That one, with eight minutes left, was a ripper at the Kop end and came after a smart assist from Florian Wirtz. Another positive there as the German had a decent game.

Over the course of this match however, Liverpool’s enduring issues were once again laid bare. As they did at Newcastle last week, Liverpool conceded bad goals. They remain too easy to play through. Isak, despite his goal, continues to look largely disconnected from the rhythms and patterns – such as they are – of his team. His goal – side footed in from a couple of yards – may help him but he – and his team – will need much more.

Put simply, Iraola’s team continue to look two or three levels below where they need to be. Last season under Arne Slot, the 2025 Premier League champions were accused of being slow, boring and with a tendency to self-harm. To a degree they still are.

Here Forest – no strangers to winning at Anfield recently or indeed in their 1970s and 1980s glory days – found space in the Liverpool half in which to play the kind of smart and incisive football that became manager Oliver Glasner’s trademark at Crystal Palace. They were impressive but Liverpool were at times shockingly complicit too.

Victor Munoz scored his first Liverpool goal to secure a 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest

Munoz struck in the closing stages with a driven effort which crashed in off the crossbar

Andoni Iraola's side have begun the season with consecutive 2-2 draws in the Premier League

New Liverpool central defender Jeremy Jacquet looks an assured footballer but Iraola’s team continues to be failed by its full-backs. One, Milos Kerkez, may yet be a Liverpool player. The other, Jeremie Frimpong, looks as though he never will. He was poor at Newcastle last week and truly pitiful here. He is a trier, but then we all know one of those don’t we?

Forest will, frankly, be disappointed not to have won. Had they done so, Liverpool could not have complained.

News of Bradley Barcola’s pending arrival had swept round Anfield before kick-off. At £123million, it feels like the kind of transfer that could go one way or the other and the truth is that Liverpool’s recent record when it comes to spending big money isn’t good. Isak and Wirtz - £225m between them – both played here with an awful lot to prove.

Liverpool do need some pace and some depth, though. The lack of both cost them dearly last season and though Munoz has given them some go-forward down the left here, there was a desperate bluntness about much of their first-half football.

There were some half chances – Munoz shot over just before half-time and Wirtz saw a header saved after rising to meet a Cody Gakpo cross. Wirtz also had a goal ruled out for offside. But there was precious little rhythm or intelligence or precision. At times, Iraola’s team resembled a group of strangers thrown together half an hour before kick-off.

Forest, on the other hand, looked well drilled and well coached and more confident in possession than maybe we would have expected given that they had lost the opening league game of Glasner’s reign at home to Leeds last weekend.

Forest have a record of doing well at Anfield and this place doesn’t scare them. Several times in the opening 20 minutes or so they worried Liverpool with the fluency and sharpness of their attacking football and when they took the lead midway through the opening half nobody inside Anfield was the slightest bit surprised.

It was a dreadful goal for Liverpool to concede, nevertheless. Newcastle cut through them from front to back to score twice on opening weekend and here the origins were to be found in a long kick downfield from Forest goalkeeper Matz Sels.

Dan Ndoye gave Nottingham Forest a first half lead with a composed finish in the box

Ndoye celebrated scoring his first Premier League goal since the opening day of last season

Alexander Isak equalised from close range following fine work from Cody Gakpo on the right

Isak opened his account for the campaign as he looks to put a nightmare debut season behind him

The Liverpool defence did manage to play a Forest forward offside but unfortunately it was the wrong one. And after Igor Jesus’s progress towards goal was halted by Alexis MacAllister, Morgan Gibbs-White picked up possession to supply Dan Ndoye and he passed the ball across Alisson and into the far corner at the Kop end with his right foot.

Ndoye had come close with a header moments before the goal while Jesus had been denied twice by blocks from Jacquet and Kerkez. Liverpool could not say they had not been warned.

Liverpool did respond with spells of possession and appeared to have equalised within a few minutes only for Frimpong to have been offside in the build up to a low shot in to the corner on the turn by Wirtz.

That was a close one and it took VAR to provide the conclusive evidence. But as Liverpool continued to play their football in a way that their ailing centre-forward Isak clearly doesn’t understand, Forest came within an Alisson fingertip of doubling their lead moments before half-time.

The Brazilian may not quite be the goalkeeper he once was but this was a magnificent save all the same. Ola Aima embarrassed Munoz at the byline to pull the ball back for Jesus and the striker’s first time shot appeared to be heading for the roof of the net before Alisson managed to divert it over with both hands.

It felt like a pivotal moment in the game and indeed it was. A two-goal deficit may have proved too much for this Liverpool team. As it was, a slow opening to the second period eventually provided Liverpool with their equaliser.

Gakpo’s turn to get rid of Forest defender Neco Williams on the edge of the penalty area was superb and his low cross found Isak lurking at the back post to slide the ball in. With half an hour yet to play, Liverpool finally had something positive to work off.

Morgan Gibbs-White restored Forest's lead from the spot, but the visitors could not hold on

Jeremie Frimpong looks like he will never make it at Liverpool with the full back struggling again

New Liverpool vice-chairman new Amir Bhatia was in attendance at Anfield on Saturday

MATCH FACTS Liverpool: (4-2-3-1): Alisson 7; Frimpong 4 (Gravenberch 71mins 6), Jacquet 7 (Araujo 76mins 6), Van Dijk 6, Kerkez 5.5 (Tsimikas 76mins 6); Szoboszlai 6, Mac Allister 6 (Nyoni 76mins 6); Gakpo 7 (Ngumoah 71mins 5.5), Wirtz 6.5, Munoz 7; Isak 6. Goals: Gakpo 60, Munoz 82mins Booked: Wirtz, Munoz, Alisson, Araujo Manager: Andoni Iraola: 6 Nottingham Forest: (3- 4-2-1) Selz 6; Cunha 6, Milenkovic 7, Murillo 7; Aina 7 (Netz 86mins 6), Schlager 7, McAtee 6 (Hudson-Odoi 90mins 6), Williams 6; Ndoye 6.5 (Delap 65mins 6.5), Gibbs-White 7; Jesus 6.5 (Dominguez 90mins 6) Goals: Ndoye 24, Gibbs-White 70 Booked: Jesus, Aina, Manager: Oliver Glasner: 7 Referee: Sam Barrott 6

It was shame, then, that nine minutes later they were behind once again. Liam Delap – a midweek buy from Chelsea – had only been on the field a few minutes when he found the Liverpool defence asleep at a throw-in and delivered the ball into Williams’ path. The former Liverpool defender couldn’t quite lift the ball over Alisson and in at the far post but he still drew a clear foul from the goalkeeper and Gibbs-White smashed in the penalty.

Defeat would have felt catastrophic for Iraola and Liverpool, especially given the presence in the directors’ box of new vice-chairman Amir Bhatia. As it was, Liverpool’s best piece of football of the new season saved them the kind of inquest that characterised last season.

Wirtz’s ball into Munoz on the edge of the penalty area in the 83rd minute was sharp but it was the Spaniard’s turn that unlocked the door. That gave Munoz space and his rising drive crashed into the net off the underside of the bar.

The late Gravenberch/Isak cameo was indicative of a larger malaise and this is Iraola’s problem to solve. His team have come perilously close to losing both of their opening games and do not yet have his coaching fingerprints on it.

The arrival of Barcola will lend Liverpool pace and star quality. It will not solve fundamental problems that have carried over from last season to this.

Sports.title: Inside Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday: How iconic football show has remained a hit 34 years after hitting TV screens
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Unpredictable. The word uttered more than any other, as I explored the inner workings of the UK's most iconic football show.

For 34 years, Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday has broadcast from their west London mega-campus, using Britain's deep footballing pyramid as the vehicle for their entertainment show.

The aforementioned unpredictability that makes it what it is. Fun, engaging, frustrating and captivating in equal measure. Because, for a football show to be worth a watch despite showing no football, there must be something that separates it from the crowd.

Sky Sports offered Daily Mail Sport exclusive, behind-the-scenes access to observe the season's first Premier League instalment of Soccer Saturday. What I found was extraordinary.

Inside the studio, hosts have changed, pundits have switched out, and the set has undergone a makeover. Outside of it the teams, managers, owners and stadiums have come and gone, but the show continues with effortless consistency.

Each day starts the same, a pre-show chat between the pundits and host, led by the producer, Kieran… which gets going as soon as Paul Merson arrives. Alongside him: Clinton Morrison, Tim Sherwood, Kris Boyd and Mike Dean.

Daily Mail Sport went behind the scenes at Soccer Saturday to see how the iconic football show is made

Simon Thomas has taken over the Soccer Saturday mantle from Jeff Stelling impeccably. He certainly has no need to fear after Daily Mail Sport's Henry Williams momentarily sat in his seat

Assembling the crew has been an unenviable task, after the likes of Matt le Tissier, Chris Kamara, Charlie Nicholas and Phil Thompson moved on. The group had a certain magic to it. Even the legendary host, Jeff Stelling, called time three years ago.

Replacing him, veteran broadcaster Simon Thomas. A Sky Sports regular for many years, trusted with replacing the man most synonymous with the show's success. Thomas has an impressive knack for conducting, yet never dominating, the conversation, leading the talent down pathways from where their opinions can flourish.

'There is literally unpredictability everywhere you look and that's the thing I love about it,' said Thomas ahead of the first Saturday of Premier League for this campaign.

'At first it's quite overwhelming because in life, we all like a little bit of control over things.

'With this show, you have no control. You're basically trying to hold on to a rudder through a very choppy sea. And the thing is to get out the other end at 5 to 6, leaving with the boats intact and me not too wet.'

As someone trying to become a sport presenter myself, I hung onto every word he told me, but it wasn't until I listened in to what he could hear in his ear that I appreciated the challenge involved in maneuvering this particular vessel.

'You've got your stats guy in your ear throughout the show who gives you little nuggets of information, especially on goalscorers, particularly when you get further down the leagues,' Thomas explains.

'You've got your producer Kieran, you've got your two directors who share the job over the course of the six hours. So there's a lot of different people talking and you've obviously got the pundits next to you.

Clinton Morrison is part of the new wave of pundits on Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday show

Paul Merson (centre) remains while Jeff Stelling, Matt Le Tissier, Phil Thompson and Charlie Nicholas have all moved on

'You're listening to what's happening in their games because you go, we're about to go to a goal in the Championship.

'But actually something's just happened in Boyd's game today. And actually we're going to go there first because he's live in the studio and update us a lot quicker, or Deano [Mike Dean] is going to look at something VAR-wise as he walks into the studio to get ready.

'So you've got to be ready to very quickly change direction.'

The show has wrestled with societal changes since its 1992 inception, when it was known as Sports Saturday.

Merson is one of the stalwarts who's stood the test of time, and has adapted his broadcasting style with immense class.

'I think at the start I was quite ruthless,' he says.

'Now you think "something's going on behind the scenes." I mean, when players lose form, they start playing poorly. There's a lot more to it than that.

'With mental health nowadays, I think you just could be a little bit more curious.

'I've rung a couple more players up. I've rung Harry Maguire up and [James] Maddison if I felt like I've said something that was a bit harsh sometimes, if I say something and afterwards, I think, "nah, that wasn't comfortable, that wasn't right."'

Merson's reflections open up broader thoughts about the show. His versatility is a wider theme that the show prides itself on. It is this versatility that is the show's greatest strength. Indeed, it has to be versatile to stay on the screen for 34 years.

The staff that work on this show week in, week out have an immense passion for what they do. They know what works, what doesn't, and how to get the best out of each other.

In an era when everyone complains about how football changes, this show welcomes the adaptability that makes it what it is.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
