NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday refuted allegations made by Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi that a "purification" ritual was performed after Mallikarjun Kharge's event in Uttarakhand, calling it a bid to divide society along caste lines.In a press conference, BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi said, "There was no caste angle to this. But as I said, they have lost their creativity, so every time they remain busy finding new ways to create conflict in India using their same worn-out lines.""And I want to ask the Congress party: If you genuinely have so much concern for the Dalit community, then on July 18, 2019, Harish Jatav was brutally attacked in Bhiwadi, and he died by suicide on August 15. Whose government was it? It was a Congress government," he added.Earlier in the day, Rahul addressed a press conference at Congress headquarters and said the incident was "another name for untouchability" and that such an act was a crime under the Constitution."Our CLP leader in Rajasthan visits a temple, and BJP leaders perform a 'purification' ritual. Congress President Kharge ji, who has dedicated his entire life to the country and the Constitution, goes to the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani to deliver a speech, and a purification ritual is performed there.Who does this? It is the people from the BJP and RSS," Rahul said."Only BJP and RSS members do this, and it is a crime. Under India's Constitution, this is a crime, a criminal activity. 'Purification' is actually just another name for untouchability. Untouchability was outlawed, yet BJP members practise it openly," he added.He also said that Dalits continue to face discrimination despite constitutional safeguards."For thousands of years, Dalits in this country have been subjected to atrocities and violence. While the Constitution made this illegal, even today, Dalit children in schools are made to clean toilets and sweep and mop floors," he said.

World.title: Union ministers Chirag Paswan, Jitan Ram Manjhi clash over quotas, demand each other's resignation
World.content:
Chirag counters HAM

How Manjhi responded

SC-ST quota row

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Two cabinet ministers - Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi - in the Narendra Modi-led government sparred over the issue of reservation on Saturday and sought each other's resignation.The controversy began after Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) president and Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi's son, Santosh Kumar Suman, sought a review of the quota policy, backing the sub-categorisation of the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and the Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the reservation regime.âI think the purpose of reservation has not been served. The concept of creating the Mahadalit category with 18 of the 22 Dalit caste groups has been defeated due to the wide gap among the beneficiaries. The Extremely Backward Classes (EBC) category was created out of the other backward castes (OBCs), and the same was true for the concept of economically weaker sections (EWS) among the upper castes,â Suman had said.âHow can it be wrong to ask which sections have benefited from reservation and to what extent, and which people standing at the very bottom of the social ladder remain deprived of it? Why is no DM or SP from the Musahar community, which has 4 percent population in Bihar? A comparative study is needed.Why will one section get 8 percent and another 80 percent among the beneficiaries?â he added.The remarks, however, did not sit well with another NDA ally, Chirag Paswan. The Union minister of food processing industries said that if Manjhi and his son want sub-quotas and a creamy layer within SC reservation, then the Union minister should resign."People ask, 'Why isn't there a 'creamy layer' provision?' Well, let them give it up, then - let them stop availing the benefits of reservation," Chirag said."If Jitan Ram Manjhi feels these measures should be implemented, should he not resign first? Let him introduce the 'creamy layer' concept - after all, he would fall under that category too, wouldn't he? He should resign, and his son - who is present here - should resign as well," he added.He also asserted that the basis of reservation lies in social factors and discussing it from an economic perspective "goes against the Constitution.""The basis is social - specifically, the issue of untouchability within society," he said.Later in the day, Jitan Ram Manjhi slammed his cabinet colleague, accusing him of not caring about poor people."People will end up being deprived of the benefits of reservation because of this stance. However, we maintain that this division is essential in the broader public interest."Since he (Chirag) does not want to look after the interests of our poor people, he should resign," he added.The controversy stems from a 2024 Supreme Court judgment that allowed states to sub-classify Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) to ensure that the benefits of reservation reach the more backward groups within these categories.It also asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the âcreamy layerâ among SCs and STs from availing reservation.The Centre, however, told the Supreme Court in an affidavit that the creamy layer principle cannot be extended to SCs and STs. It said the principle currently applies only to Other Backward Classes (OBCs)."It has nowhere specifically been held that the principle of creamy layer is applicable to SCs and STs. The reference made to the concept of creamy layerâ¦ appears to be the general observation with regard to reservation in respect of OBCs (Other Backward Classes)/SEBCs (Socially and Educationally Backward Classes)."

World.title: Nepal floods: MEA says 88 Indians rescued, 287 still missing; forensic teams dispatched
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Saturday said that 88 Indian nationals have been rescued so far, while 287 remain missing amid the devastating floods in Nepal.

It added that 128 persons of Indian origin are also reported missing. Moreover, the death toll from the floods has risen to 669.

Four Indian nationals, Ripu Kumar, Chaneshwar Narzary, Kripa Shankar and Mohammed Minhajuddin, were rescued from a hydropower project in Rasuwa on Saturday and are expected to reach Kathmandu shortly.

World.title: From 'khana bana leti ho' to 'will our lives fit together?' How India's marriage biodata is evolving
World.content:
Every year, India witnesses a familiar wave - the marriage season. Wedding halls fill up, families revive old contacts, matrimonial apps see a surge, and somewhere between the âladka kya karta hai?â and âladki ko kya pasand hai?â, the search for a perfect match begins.

India records approximately 10 million marriages a year, or roughly 30,000 weddings a day, according to BiodataPlus.in.

Amid the rituals, celebrations and matchmaking conversations comes a quieter ritual: the biodata.

What looks like a simple one-page profile is, in fact, a snapshot of a changing India, reflecting what families still look for, what young Indians now expect from a partner and how the idea of a âgood matchâ is being rewritten.

The old marriage checklist

For years, a marriage biodata followed an almost predictable template: age, height, complexion, caste, salary and family background.

For women, descriptions such as âfairâ, âhomelyâ and âwell-manneredâ were not unusual. For men, a stable job, income, property and family status often carried considerable weight.

Recalling her experience, 52-year-old Mamata from Uttar Pradesh, told TOI these factors continue to play a major role in rural areas, although expectations have evolved as one moves towards urban India. âDuring my time, a few family members used to visit the girlâs family and ask questions about her height, age, hobbies and, most importantly, whether she could cook (

khana bana leti ho?

). The girlâs family wasnât really allowed to ask questions to the other side.





That used to be a very awkward conversation,â she said.

But she sees a clear difference in how the next generation approaches marriage.

âMy daughter has her own perspective and priorities. If parents of my generation were looking for a match for her, we would consider the factors I mentioned above. But those things may not matter to my daughter because she is working and living abroad,â she said.

The difference, then, may not simply be about what appears on a biodata.

It is also about who gets to decide what matters.

Whatâs changed, and what hasnât

So, has the marriage biodata itself really changed?

Not really.

Shalini Singh, founder of matchmaking platform Andwemet, believes the format has remained surprisingly similar, even as expectations around marriage have evolved.

âHonestly, the biodata format itself hasn't changed much because what needs to change is the mindset of the people creating them. That kind of change is hard, but it's the only way forward.

And the people who are willing to evolve their biodata are the ones finding better matches,â she said.

Relationship coach Sidhharrth S Kumaar of NumroVani sees the shift less in the document itself and more in its purpose.

According to him, the question is gradually moving from âIs this family socially suitable?â to âCan these two individuals realistically build a life together?â

He also points to a change in who controls the process. While parents were once the primary custodians of marriage biodatas, individuals are increasingly taking charge of their own profiles and decisions, sometimes with guidance from relationship or matrimonial coaches and even AI.

âParents use the biodata to reduce social uncertainty, while their children use it to reduce relationship uncertainty,â noted Kumaar.

That distinction captures one of the biggest changes in the modern marriage search.

Verona Matchmaking, another platform TOI spoke to, points to another broader shift: the changing role of courtship itself. Young Indians increasingly want the opportunity to date, spend time together and genuinely get to know each other before deciding to marry.

Which was yes- not a case earlier.

But there is an interesting contradiction. As people become better at describing exactly what they want in a partner, there is also a risk of becoming too good at filtering people out.

Verona Matchmaking therefore emphasises the importance of keeping an open mind during the process. The objective, it suggests, âshould not be to find someone who perfectly matches every item on a checklist, but to find someone worth getting to know.â

From 'fitting in' to 'fitting together'

For people currently looking for a partner, the shift is increasingly visible in the questions they ask.

Rupali Rani, an account manager at The Reppro who is currently looking for a match, told TOI that financial stability is important but no longer enough. âFor me, financial stability is only one part of the picture. I want to know how a person thinks, communicates, treats people and looks at life. I would rather have a good conversation with someone and realise that our values align than tick ten boxes on a biodata and then struggle to have a conversation in real life,â she said.

For Rani, the change is particularly visible in what women expect from marriage. âIt is now less about âWill you fit into my family?â and more about âWill our lives fit together?ââ she said.

âI would rather have an uncomfortable conversation in the beginning than a comfortable misunderstanding that becomes a problem later. My career, my lifestyle and my independence are important to me. Of course, being in a relationship means making adjustments; both people will have to.

But adjustment and compromise are not the same thing,â she added.

Data cited by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) also points to broader changes in womenâs lives.

In India, efforts to delay girlsâ marriage have contributed to a decline in marriages before the age of 18, from 47% in 2006 to 23% in 2019-2021. Over the same period, the proportion of girls completing higher secondary education increased from 34% to 48%.

The other side

But women aren't the only ones rewriting the rules of modern matchmaking. Men, too, are pushing back against transactional evaluations in search of genuine emotional alignment.

Shivam Sharma, who is currently looking for a match, told TOI that questions about his CTC, job, property, family responsibilities and career plans are common, particularly from the prospective brideâs family.

He understands why families ask such questions but believes a man's worth should not be reduced to his income or assets.

âSomeone may have a very high salary or own properties worth crores, but that doesn't guarantee that he will be a good husband, that he will bring happiness to his partner, or that the relationship will be free from dishonesty or conflicts,â he said.

Instead, Sharma believes families should also ask about a manâs ambitions, values, work ethic, financial plans and how he views his responsibilities towards his family.

He also sees a change in who gets the final say.

âBoth families may still be involved, but ultimately, the decision is increasingly being left to the two people who are actually going to spend their lives together. I think that is an important and positive change,â he said.

Traditional expectations from women, however, have not disappeared. Sharma said terms such as âgood familyâ and âhomelyâ can still influence matchmaking, but personally, he does not consider appearance-based factors such as height or fairness important.

âFor me, good nature, mutual understanding, compatibility and family values matter much more than someone's appearance,â he said.

He also does not expect his future wife to give up her ambitions, friendships, interests or individuality after marriage.

âIf she wants to travel, spend time with her friends, watch a movie, go on a long drive or pursue something that makes her happy, I don't think marriage should stop her from doing those things.

She should have her own space and freedom, just as I would expect to have mine,â he said.

Major decisions, including family planning, should also be discussed and taken jointly, he added.

âMarriage should involve adjustments from both sides, not sacrifices expected from only one person,â Sharma said.

Biodata vs person

For those who have gone through matchmaking, the importance of a biodata can look different in hindsight. What seems important while searching for a partner may not always matter once two people begin building a life together.

Vaibhavi Srivastava, an assistant account manager in corporate communications and PR, and Prakhar Mathur, a software test engineer, are now married. Speaking to TOI, they shared what they looked for in each other's biodatas and how their idea of a âgood matchâ has evolved.

Srivastava focused more on the individual than the family. She looked for educational qualifications, career, future plans and a progressive, open-minded partner who would support her ambitions.

A relatively small family was also a preference.

Mathur initially considered age, but soon focused on personality, education and career goals. He liked that Srivastava had âher own goals and clear ideas regarding her futureâ.

For both, compatibility and mutual support mattered more than ticking boxes. Srivastava now places greater emphasis on family values and communication, while Mathur believes biodatas reveal only so much.

âReal priorities will come to the fore during a conversation about your way of communication and your view of life,â he said.

Neither considered caste or family status deciding factors. Ultimately, they said, the relationship is between the two people getting married.

The old checklist is evolving â¦ slowly

Yet the shift towards compatibility does not mean the traditional marriage checklist has disappeared. Caste, complexion, height, income and family background continue to influence partner selection, though their importance varies across families and generations.

Sharma believes caste still matters, but the barrier is thinner than it was for his parents' generation. Greater interaction through education, workplaces and social circles, he said, has made young people more open to cross-caste relationships.

âI don't think caste has disappeared, but I do think compatibility, understanding and individual choice are becoming more important,â he said, adding that marriage decisions are increasingly about the two people rather than their caste backgrounds.

Rani sees a similar transition. Preferences for someone âfairâ, âhomelyâ or from a âgood familyâ remain, she said, even as others prioritise stable careers, emotional maturity and shared values.

âWe are in a transition phase. The old checklist hasn't disappeared; it has simply started sharing space with a new one,â she said.

Ankur Gola, a resident of Delhi, who recently got married, told TOI, âmy family was on board with whoever I'm considering but there was an orthodox condition that person should not be of lower cast or muslim; which was difficult for me to accept as they never taught me to discriminate against people...

I decided to break the cycle.â

New words, old biases

Sidhharrth Kumaar takes the argument a step further. He believes traditional factors have not necessarily disappeared, they have sometimes simply been given newer names.

Caste, he said, may be described as âcultural compatibilityâ or âsimilar traditionsâ. Complexion and appearance may become âpresentableâ, âwell-groomedâ or âfitness-consciousâ, while family status may appear as âsimilar upbringingâ, âcompatible lifestyleâ or âwell-settled familyâ.

Even the phrase âour vibes did not matchâ, he said, can sometimes become a convenient umbrella for discomfort related to appearance, accent, class, caste-coded habits or family culture without explicitly naming the criterion.

âThese expressions are not inherently discriminatory, but they can camouflage older preferences. The language of matchmaking has modernised faster than the underlying selection criteria,â he said.

The transition, therefore, is not a clean break from the past.

The vocabulary of matchmaking may be changing, but some of the old filters continue to quietly shape who gets considered a âgood matchâ.

The big picture

The traditional one-page marriage biodata is no longer confined to a printed sheet passed between relatives, family friends or neighbours.

Increasingly, matchmaking has moved online, with profiles becoming searchable, editable and instantly shareable.

That has changed the reach of the biodata.

What once travelled through a limited family or community network can now be shared far beyond it, sometimes with hundreds or thousands of potential matches.

Yet technology has not necessarily erased tradition.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Instead, the old checklist has found a new home online.

A profile can still ask about caste, family, profession and income, even as it increasingly includes interests, lifestyle, career aspirations and expectations from a partner.

The format has become digital. The conversation around it is becoming more personal.

And perhaps that is the real evolution of the Indian marriage biodata.

It is no longer only asking, âIs this person suitable for our family?â

Increasingly, the question is becoming:

âCan these two people build a life that works for both of them?â

The biodata may still fit on one page. But the definition of a âgood matchâ is getting much bigger.

World.title: ‘Do ministers feed their own children expired food?’ Abhijeet Dipke during ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign
World.content:
Abhijeet Dipke raises questions during campaign

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke visited villages in Maharashtraâs Hingoli district as part of his âSchool Thik Karoâ campaign, inspecting government schools and raising concerns over the condition of school infrastructure and the quality of food supplies used for midday meals.Speaking about his findings, Dipke said, "I was absolutely shocked by what I saw this morning. The food items being used for the midday meal were expiredâthey had gone past their expiry date six or seven months ago. I want to ask the ministers, MLAs, and officialsâdo they feed their own children expired food?"He also raised concerns about basic facilities in government schools, alleging that several schools lacked drinking water, usable washrooms, benches and adequate teaching staff."Even after all these years, if children in our country's government schools lack drinking water and usable restrooms and have to sit on the floor because there are no benchesâthen what exactly has been done?" Dipke said."Only when the government supports these children and builds good schools for them will they be able to achieve something in life," he added.Dipke further said, "None of the schools have drinking water, and none of them have washrooms.None of the schools have benches for children to sit on, nor do they have enough teachers."During his visit to Kadoli village, Dipke said he found a school building that had been constructed in 1950 and claimed that no work had been carried out on it since then."When I visited Kadoli village, I saw a building that had been constructed back in 1950. No work had been done on that building since 1950," he said.Dipke alleged that political interests were being prioritised over the needs of children, saying, "Their only priority is gaining power by any means necessary."Dipke had launched the campaign on August 15 from his native village, Santuk Pipri, and returned to the area to inspect schools in Lohgaon, Karanjal, Jamdaya, Jambhrun and Khillar.Dipke had earlier said the campaign would be expanded to other talukas across Maharashtra before being taken nationwide as a social-audit exercise involving parents and local communities. The initiative has also drawn attention beyond the state.In Rajasthan, authorities recently barred outsiders from entering government-school premises without prior permission and prohibited photography, videography, interviews and live streaming inside schools. However, officials have not explicitly linked the restrictions to Dipkeâs campaign.Dipke is seeking to turn individual complaints about government schools into a broader accountability campaign, arguing that meaningful improvement will require officials, politicians and local communities to confront the conditions in schools firsthand.

World.title: ‘UP no longer Bimaru state’: CM Yogi says mafia crushed, encephalitis eradicated; Akhilesh flags gaps
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief minister

on Saturday said the state had shed its image as a âBimaruâ state and now commanded a ârespectable imageâ, citing improvements in healthcare, connectivity, education and law and order.

His remarks in Deoria came as

chief

Akhilesh Yadav

separately attacked the BJP government over the condition of the state's healthcare system, alleging shortages of doctors and paramedical staff.

CM Yogi targets previous governments

Addressing a programme in Deoria, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 80 development projects worth Rs 305 crore, Yogi accused previous Samajwadi Party and Congress governments of remaining indifferent to

encephalitis

deaths.

âEncephalitis was not merely a disease; it was a sick mindset. It was the sick mentality of the Samajwadi Party and Congress governments of that time -- a mentality that was devouring the innocent lives here while the authorities remained completely indifferent,â Adityanath said, according to news agency ANI.

He claimed that more than 50,000 innocent lives were lost over four decades and alleged that no chief minister from the Samajwadi Party or Congress, or Congress prime minister, had visited the region to assess the situation.





Adityanath also alleged that a parallel âmafia ruleâ had operated across Uttar Pradesh under previous governments.

âA parallel mafia rule operated across the state. Today, I can say that UP has truly lived up to its name. No one calls UP a 'Bimaru' state anymore. No one questions Uttar Pradesh now. The state now commands a respectable image,â he said.

âThe mafia has been crushed, wiped out completely. For those who threaten the safety of daughters and traders, there are only two places: either jail or hell; there is no third option,â he added.

The chief minister said the government had moved from âone district, one mafiaâ to âone district, one medical collegeâ, pointing to medical colleges in Deoria and Kushinagar.

Deoria development projects , education and connectivity

Adityanath said encephalitis had been eradicated and linked the development to the government's healthcare initiatives.

He highlighted the medical college in Deoria named after Maharishi Deoraha Baba and said connectivity in the district was being improved through new bypasses and flyovers.

âSingle-lane roads are being converted to double lanes, double-lane roads to 4-lanes, and 4-lane roads to 6-lanes,â he said.

The chief minister also highlighted composite schools, the upgradation of Kasturba Gandhi schools, Abhyudaya coaching facilities for competitive examinations and the transformation of basic education schools under the government's âOperation Kayakalpâ programme.

Akhilesh alleges shortages in healthcare system

Separately, Akhilesh Yadav alleged that Uttar Pradesh was facing shortages of doctors and paramedical staff and promised free treatment and medicines for poor people if the Samajwadi Party returned to power.

Yadav claimed there was one doctor for every 16,000 people in the state and alleged that 41% of posts in government hospitals were vacant.

âMore than 24,000 posts in nursing and paramedical services are vacant,â he said.

The former chief minister also claimed that 604 posts were vacant at AIIMS Gorakhpur and 579 at AIIMS Rae Bareli.

World.title: Two killed, SI injured in Suryapet over dispute involving tree
World.content:
Two persons were killed in a double murder at Erragattu Thanda in Mellacheruvu mandal of Suryapet district on Saturday, with police attributing the incident to a long-standing dispute and personal animosity between neighbours.

Suryapet district SP Narasimha, along with DSP Srinivas Reddy and other police personnel, inspected the scene and spoke to the victims’ family members. He said the police would conduct a thorough investigation and ensure that strong evidence was placed before the court for swift and severe punishment of those responsible.

According to the SP, Bhukya Pedababu, Bhukya Ramu and their mother, who were neighbours of the victims, allegedly attacked Amaraboyina Venkateswarlu and his father. Both victims sustained critical injuries and died at the spot. The incident reportedly followed a dispute involving a tree.

A case has been registered against Pedababu, Ramu and their mother based on eyewitness accounts and preliminary evidence. Ramakrishnareddy, In-charge CI of Kodad Rural, has been appointed as the investigating officer.

The SP said Pedababu had previously worked as a physics teacher but was suspended over alleged behavioural issues and violations of rules. There had also been previous complaints accusing him of frequently instigating disputes and filing petitions that caused unrest in the village, he said.

The bodies were examined at the Government Hospital in Huzurnagar. Police urged residents to maintain peace and not take the law into their own hands.

World.title: G. Vijaya Raghavan, P.P. Balan among four members appointed to Kerala State Planning Board
World.content:
The State government has appointed four members to the Kerala State Planning Board including former technocrat G. Vijaya Raghavan and local governance expert P.P. Balan.

The other two members are environmentalist Sridhar Radhakrishnan andNew Delhi-based Varun Santhosh, the Planning and Economic Affairs department said in an August 29 order. This is Mr. Vijaya Raghavan’s third stint as a Planning Board member. Mr. Balan was a former Director of the Kerala Institute of Local Administration (KILA).

The appointments have been made in the “interest of strengthening the board’s advisory and planning capacity,” the department said.

In July, the UDF government had reconstituted the Planning Board with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan as the chairperson and former Union Cabinet Secretary K.M. Chandrasekhar as the vice-chairperson. And in August, the State government appointed D. Narayana, former Director, Gulati Institute of Finance and Taxation (GIFT), as Senior Economic Advisor and Kiran Kumar Kakarlapudi, Assistant Professor, GIFT, and M. Parameswaran, Professor, Centre for Development Studies, as Economic Advisors to Mr. Chandrasekhar.

The appointments are keenly watched given the UDF government’s plans to transform the Planning Board into a ‘think tank’ for the government. The first recommendation in this regard had come in the White Paper laid in the State Assembly in June. The suggestion also featured in the Revised Budget for the 2026-27 fiscal. The proposal has drawn flak from the Opposition LDF which alleged that the government was aping the BJP government, which had replaced the Planning Commission with the NITI Aayog.

However, in a written reply to the State Legislative Assembly on July 1 this year, Mr. Satheesan said that the Planning Board ,“which plays a crucial role in the State’s development”, and the five-year plans will be continued.

World.title: Sullia MLA urges government to take elephant attacks seriously
World.content:
Sullia MLA Bhagirathi Murulya said on Saturday that the menace of elephants in Sullia and surrounding areas has emerged as a major problem for farmers, and urged the government to take serious measures to protect agricultural lands from attacks.

Speaking at the District Development Co-ordination and Monitoring Committee (DISHA) meeting, the MLA said the government should install solar-powered electric fencing system to prevent elephant raids. While the government currently provides a 50% subsidy to farmers for solar fencing, she urged the State to bear the entire cost. She noted that farmers are already suffering financial distress due to yellow leaf disease, fruit rot disease, and leaf spot disease in arecanut plantations.

A Forest Department official informed the meeting that an estimated 80 elephants are currently roaming the Sullia and Puttur areas. The department has distributed ₹3.30 lakh in compensation to 19 farmers for crop destruction so far this year. Additionally, compensation of ₹73 lakh is yet to be disbursed to 381 farmers.

Deputy Commissioner H.V. Darshan directed the Forest Department to register a case against GAIL Mangalore Petrochemicals Ltd. (GMPL) for burying a dead peacock without informing the department. Earlier, Bajpe Town Panchayat president Lokesh Poojary had raised the issue, stating that GMPL authorities in the Mangaluru Special Economic Zone had buried the peacock without notifying the Forest Department. He said that despite the town panchayat filing a complaint, no action had been taken against the company.

A Forest Department official clarified that no case was registered initially as company authorities pleaded ignorance of the law. However, the department later exhumed the carcass and conducted a post-mortem examination.

Mr. Darshan remarked that ignorance of the law is no excuse, directing officials to register an FIR and investigate whether the bird was poisoned.

World.title: Will send team to Nepal if MEA gives permission: West Bengal CM
World.content:
Kolkata

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said late on Friday night (August 28, 2026) that the State Government would send a team to Nepal to assist in rescue and relief operations if it received permission from the Ministry of External Affairs.

“I have asked the Chief Secretary to seek permission from the MEA to send our delegation to Nepal, which will include one Minister, one MLA, one IG-rank police officer, and a senior IAS officer of secretary or joint secretary level. Once we get permission, we will move them to Kathmandu,” Mr. Adhikari said.

Citing official records, he said that of the 39 people from West Bengal reported missing in Nepal, the State Government has managed to contact two and is arranging for their early return. They are Anukul Poddar and his wife (name not published yet). Both are aged above 60 and are from Basirhat. The remaining 37 are still untraced.

“Many families have heard that some people have been rescued on the Tibet side. We have assured the families that we are trying to gather a list of those names,” Mr. Adhikari said.

CM speaks to families

On Friday night (August 28, 2026), the Chief Minister also spoke with the families of the missing persons over a video call and assured them of all possible help in rescuing their loved ones. The video call, held from Bhawani Bhawan, the State police headquarters, was also attended by several senior police officials.

During the meeting, the families raised concerns about the rescue and relief operations and sought information on ways to track updates on their relatives.

Among the 37 people still missing from West Bengal, 32 had embarked on the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra with Kolkata-based travel agency “Cholo Jai”. Of them, 30 were tourists, including at least 21 senior citizens, while two were tour operators.

One of those reported missing is Sharmistha Bhowmik Roy, daughter-in-law of former Union Minister Mukul Roy.

Her husband, Subhrangshu Roy, a former MLA and Mukul Roy’s son, told media persons that the families of those missing have now become like one family as they wait for their loved ones to return home.

A delegation of senior Trinamool Congress leaders also met Subhrangshu Roy on Saturday (August 29, 2026). Mukul Roy, one of the founding members of the party, passed away a few months ago.

World.title: Nepal floods: ‘Bodies buried in slush, families refusing food’, Khalsa Aid volunteers witness devastation
World.content:
Thick slush swallowing houses, roads turned treacherous, the stench of decomposing bodies of people and animals hanging in the air, and army camps transformed into makeshift mortuaries where ambulances arrive carrying the dead — these are scenes from Nepal’s flood-ravaged valleys, as described by Khalsa Aid volunteers working in the worst-hit areas.

For these volunteers who have spent the past three days moving through the affected areas, the devastation along Nepal’s border with Tibet is difficult to comprehend. In Nuwakot, Rasuwa and Dhading, entire stretches of villages and markets have been buried under mud and debris after a sudden flood tore through the mountain valleys.

“Today, if you go, you will not see water. But there is a lot of slush. Buildings are fully submerged in it. Many bodies are buried inside this,” said Manohar Naidu, a Bengaluru native who is currently in Nuwakot with Khalsa Aid.

“Even when we are trying to walk on the sides, we are slipping into the slush. The entire area is now stinking because of all the dead bodies of humans and animals. The situation on the ground is really bad,” Mr. Naidu said.

The disaster began on Wednesday (August 26) when a section of a Himalayan glacier collapsed near the Nepal-China border, sending a mass of ice, rock and debris into the Lhende river system. The resulting surge swept through Nepal’s Rasuwa district before moving downstream into Nuwakot and Dhading.

By Saturday (August 29), the scale of the catastrophe had become clearer. At least 676 people had died in Nepal and Tibet, while nearly 2,400 remained missing. More than 3,700 people had been rescued in Nepal, but large parts of the affected terrain remained difficult to reach because roads and bridges had been destroyed.

For those on the ground, however, the numbers do little to capture what the disaster looks and smells like.

In Rasuwa and Nuwakot, army camps have been turned into temporary mortuaries as hospital morgues run out of space. The volunteers described convoys of ambulances arriving with bodies recovered from the debris, which are being kept at the camps in the interim before being sent for identification.

Outside the tents, families wait in desperation.

Some have spent hours standing in the hope of receiving news about relatives who disappeared when the flood came. Mr. Naidu said many families have refused even the hot food - including rice, lentils, curries, being offered by volunteers.

“They are not even willing to accept the food that we are offering them. All they want to know is about their loved ones,” he said.

“Those who are with families are still eating a little. Those who have lost their loved ones aren’t even willing to eat at all,” said Manpreet Singh, a volunteer from Patiala, Punjab.

Mr. Singh, who has also worked during floods in Assam and a cyclone in Tamil Nadu, travelled to Nepal with five other volunteers from Punjab.

Their team recently reached Gajuri Bajar in Dhading, where they saw a large market area that had been almost completely washed away.

“Locals told us the market was active and full of people when the flood came. A lot of people were washed away and thousands remain missing still,” he said.

The volunteers had initially been assisting with rescue operations and the identification of bodies alongside the Lions Club, but on Saturday (August 29) were told by the authorities that rescue operations would be handled by the army and external organisations would not be allowed to take them up.

Their role has consequently shifted towards relief and support for those waiting at military camps for news of relatives. Khalsa Aid volunteers are currently providing hot meals, clothes and basic medical assistance at relief camps. One camp in Nuwakot is sheltering around 400 people, who are being looked after by volunteers.

Among the people Mr. Singh met was a 16-year-old girl who survived because her family received a warning moments before the flood struck.

“Her father received a call telling him that the flood was coming and that they should leave the house. She was studying at that time. The family ran to safety. Had they stayed, they too could have been swept away. Now she has lost all hope and we don’t know how to even encourage them,” he said.

The warning, however, came too late for many others.

Entire houses now stand disconnected from the road and filled with mud. In some places, there is barely a patch of firm ground on which to stand. Animal carcasses also remain scattered across the affected areas, adding to the stench.

The devastation has also left remote communities cut off from food and assistance. Mr. Naidu said some villages remain inaccessible because roads, bridges and other links have been destroyed. Khalsa Aid has proposed adopting some of these villages and supporting them through the rehabilitation process, but is awaiting a response from the Nepalese authorities.

The organisation is also expanding its presence. At present, its team comprises volunteers from Nepal and India, while three teams from India, Kenya and U.K. are expected to arrive on Sunday (August 30). The volunteers on the ground are assessing what individual communities need so that larger quantities of relief material can be sent in the coming days.

In some communities, however, people have asked for something different from cooked food.

Mr. Naidu said some Buddhist residents have been reluctant to accept prepared meals and have instead asked for raw ingredients so they can cook according to their own practices.

World.title: 11-day Velankanni annual feast begins as a sea of devotees throngs the Basilica
World.content:
The annual festival of Our Lady of Good Health at Velankanni in Nagapattinam district commenced on Saturday evening with a flag procession followed by the blessing and hoisting of Our Lady’s Flag by Most Rev. T. Sagayaraj, Bishop of Thanjavur Diocese.

A large number of pilgrims from across the country thronged the Basilica to attend the 11-day festival. Rev. Fr. C. Irudayaraj, Rector; parish priest, and clergy of the Thanjavur Diocese accompanied the Bishop in leading the procession.

The flag-hoisting was followed by the litany, benediction, and Holy Mass in Tamil at the Shrine auditorium.

On September 7, the rosary, litany, and novena prayer, will be followed by a concelebrated Holy Mass and Our Lady’s car procession to be presided over by the Bishop. A special feast mass will be conducted on September 8 in the Lower Basilica to commemorate the birth anniversary of Mother Mary. The feast will conclude with the lowering of Our Lady’s flag in the evening.

During the festival days, services will be held in Tamil, English, Marathi, Konkani, Malayalam, Telugu, Kannada, and Hindi. The car procession of Our Lady of Health will be taken out on all novena days at 8 p.m.

With thousands of pilgrims expected to attend the festival, elaborate security arrangements have been made. Four Deputy Superintendents of Police, 2,432 police personnel, and 378 traffic police personnel have been deployed. Surveillance has been strengthened with 15 watchtowers, three drone cameras, and 300 CCTV cameras. A 24-hour control room has been established to coordinate emergency response.

An integrated control room has been set up to provide immediate assistance to devotees. Around seven special medical camps have been established, with 21 doctors, 52 health inspectors, and 21 nurses deployed for duty. Three two-wheeler ambulances, and 10 emergency ambulances have been stationed at various locations.

The Fire and Rescue Services Department has deployed 12 vehicles as part of the safety arrangements. A team of five personnel will conduct rotational surveillance using two boats, while six local swimmers have been deployed to monitor the sea and ensure the safety of pilgrims on the beach.

Drinking water will be supplied through 1,000-litre tanks at 10 locations. A team of 40 personnel has been formed to carry out chlorination. Sanitation arrangements have been strengthened, with eight health inspectors, eight sanitation supervisors, and 425 sanitation workers deployed for duty.

Special buses

Meanwhile, the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation, Kumbakonam, will operate 4,230 special buses to and from Velankanni until September 9, throughout the day and night.

These special buses will operate to and from Velankanni, connecting major towns, including Chennai, Dindigul, Madurai, Tiruchi, Manapparai, Thanjavur, Kumbakonam, Poondi Matha Church, Oriyur, Chidambaram, Puducherry, Mayiladuthurai, Pattukkottai, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Nagore, and Karaikal.

World.title: Karnataka: Medical college hospital gets ₹5.5 crore ICMR grant for rare skin disorder research
World.content:
The Sri Madhusudan Sai Institute of Medical Sciences and Research (SMSIMSR), located at Muddenahalli in Chickballapur district, has received a ₹5.5-crore research grant from the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to develop affordable diagnostic and precision treatment approaches for epidermolysis bullosa (EB), a rare genetic disorder that causes extreme skin fragility.

The ₹5,50,08,874 grant, awarded for four years, will support the ADAPT-EB project — Developing Accessible Diagnostics and Affordable Precision Therapies for Epidermolysis Bullosa in the Indian population. The project will be led by doctors Vamsi Krishna Yenamandra, with Divya Seshadri and Manoj Srinivasa of SMSIMSR, and Sharath Chandra Konda of SVS Medical College, Mahbubnagar, as co-investigators.

EB comprises a group of inherited disorders in which minor friction or trauma can cause blistering and wounds. Patients can develop chronic wounds, scarring, nutritional complications and an increased risk of skin cancer.

The project seeks to address gaps in diagnosis and treatment in India, where there is currently no national EB registry and access to affordable molecular diagnostics, and coordinated multidisciplinary care remains limited, according to SMSIMSR.

Focus on affordable diagnosis

One of the key objectives is to develop low-cost targeted genomic assays that could reduce diagnostic costs by more than 60% compared with whole-exome sequencing. The tests are also expected to have applications in identifying carriers and prenatal screening.

The researchers will also study “revertant mosaicism”, a naturally occurring genetic self-correction seen in some cells, to explore its potential in developing patient-specific regenerative therapies.

Integrated precision medicine approach

The researchers said the project would bring prevention, prediction, diagnosis, regenerative therapy and genotype-guided disease management into a single framework.

The aim is to generate evidence that can support earlier diagnosis, improve genetic counselling and make therapeutic options more accessible to people with EB in India.

Dr. Yenamandra said EB posed a major challenge to patients and families, particularly when specialised diagnosis and care were difficult to access. “ADAPT-EB is designed to address this gap,” he said.

World.title: Chennai Corporation Council meeting | Unlikely allies as parties unite against State govt. over lack of ward funds
World.content:
Councillors of different political parties extended support to the DMK in criticising the State government for not releasing the ward development funds, at the Greater Corporation Corporation (GCC) Council meeting on Friday.

The councillors, including those from the Congress, the AIADMK, and the BJP, also raised concerns over cancelled tenders, gaps in the stormwater drain network, and poor road conditions. DMK’s floor leader, N. Ramalingam, moved a resolution seeking special funds — ₹60 crore for each ward — from the State government for ward development works.

Ward 141 councillor A. Raja Anbazhagan, who contested the 2026 Assembly election as the DMK candidate from T. Nagar, said councillors should consider resigning before the next Council meeting if the ward development funds were not released.

Later, BJP councillor Uma Anandan, who wore black in support of the resolution, said even capital funds were not released. “We [councillors] are not asking for cars for ourselves, but for funds to implement projects. After working for all these months, we are unable to complete projects in the last leg due to the lack of funds,” she said.

“I want to implement flood mitigation works on Subba Reddy Street. I also intend to link the stormwater drain in Ellaiamman Koil Street with the one near Madley Road Subway to mitigate flooding. But the GCC has not allocated funds for the past five months. Does the State government know its priorities?” she added.

AIADMK councillor T. Sathyanathan said funds had been disbursed uniformly in the past four years, but were not being released now, which was condemnable.

Councillors from the CPI and the CPI(M), M. Renuka and R. Jayaraman, supported the demand. Mr. Jayaraman criticised GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran for allegedly “blocking the release of ward development funds”. Councillors from the MDMK, VCK, and Manithaneya Makkal Katchi also supported the resolution.

Standing Committee (Works) chairperson N. Chitararasu, who contested the 2026 Assembly election as the DMK candidate from Anna Nagar, said the State government was withholding funds because it feared that the DMK could win the forthcoming local body elections. Valasaravakkam ward committee chairperson V. Rajan questioned whether the current regime was democratic or bureaucratic, and said councillors may hold a hunger strike if the situation continued.

DMK councillor for K.K. Nagar K. Karna said several emergency works undertaken using ward-level funds were stalled and that the TVK government must be held responsible in case there was more stagnation this monsoon.

Manali DMK councillor A. Rajendran said the tenders for the flood management centre in his ward were cancelled, roads were not re-laid due to high bitumen prices, and a community hall in Sadayankuppam needed an overhaul.

Deputy Mayor M. Magesh Kumaar, referring to the GCC’s financial constraints and the lack of progress in projects for which foundation stones were laid by former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, said the Corporation should consider providing maternity and menstrual leave to the protesting National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM) workers. He said, “The State now boasts the smooth functioning of the Amma Unavagams across the city. It was the GCC that earlier allocated ₹100 crore to ensure this.”

Mayor R. Priya said the Council would formally register its dissatisfaction with the State government, and a resolution urging it to take note of the Council’s demand would be passed.

“Only if the funds are released now can the works be scheduled and completed within six to seven months... earlier, over 100 resolutions would be passed, but now barely 30 have been passed, and that too pertaining to the dispersal of pension and the maintenance or deployment of temporary NULM workers,” she said.

She also insisted that the Commissioner issue a circular to the zonal officials to coordinate with the councillors and chairpersons regarding projects, inspections, and civic works at the meeting.

Will take to CM’s notice: Congress

Tiruvottiyur councillor and leader of 13 Congress councillors in the GCC M. Samuel Diraviam, supporting the resolution, said he would take the issue to the notice of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.

Meanwhile, Alwarthirunagar councillor V.V. Giridharan, who had recently declared that he had joined the TVK, said the councillor fund that he had saved from last year could be used to complete the setting up of a health and wellness centre in the ward, in case capital funds could not be disbursed.

World.title: Pims fire: PM Shehbaz orders suspension, criminal action against 8 officials as inquiry panel submits interim report
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday ordered the suspension of eight officials, including the executive director (ED) of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), and directed that criminal proceedings be initiated against them over a fire at the hospital that claimed the lives of 14 infants.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the premier took the decision on the recommendations of the inquiry committee, whose interim report was presented at a high-level meeting chaired by him in Lahore.

The eight individuals are namely Pims ED Dr Rana Imran Sikander, Joint Executive Directors Dr Mutahir Shah and Dr Chaudhry Awais Ali Shah, head of neonatal department Prof Dr Sadia Riaz, senior registrar Dr Nagham, Dr Naushila Amjad, Pims Security Assistant Director Mohammad Usman, and Dr Abdulrehman, the director general of the Emergency Services of the Capital Development Authority (CDA).

The prime minister specifically directed that those identified by the inquiry committee face not only departmental action but also criminal proceedings under the relevant laws, the PMO said.

He also ordered that criminal proceedings be initiated against those responsible without discrimination and approved action against the company tasked with providing security at the hospital and its officials.

The premier further directed that National Institutes of Health (NIH) Chief Executive Officer Dr Mohammad Salman be appointed acting executive director of Pims. He also ordered the immediate appointment of new officials to replace those removed from their positions.

The prime minister appointed another nurse present in the ward and a female guard as officers on special duty (OSDs) and directed further investigation into the incident.

He also directed the immediate release of the inquiry committee’s preliminary report, the PMO said, adding that the document would be published on the health ministry’s website.

Speaking on the occasion, the premier said those responsible for criminal negligence would not be given any leniency and vowed that those responsible for the incident would be brought to justice.

“The deaths of these innocent children are a heartbreaking tragedy that has left the entire nation grieving. My sympathies, along with those of the entire nation, are with the children’s parents,” he said.

Shehbaz added that those responsible would be given exemplary punishment to ensure that no mother was separated from her child again because of criminal negligence.

Inquiry report

The interim report of the inquiry committee was presented at the meeting, which was also shown CCTV footage of the incident lasting approximately two minutes.

The initial findings showed that Pims had no detailed standard operating procedures (SOPs) or training for dealing with fires or other emergency situations. Of the hospital’s 13 SOPs, references to fire or emergency situations were found in only two subsections, the meeting was told.

Supervisory staff were not on duty when the incident occurred. Two nurses, a female guard and a house officer were present in the ward at the time, according to the briefing.

The fire broke out and engulfed the entire ward within two minutes. One nurse saved a child’s life before the flames spread through the ward, risking her own safety in the process.

An emergency services call was made six minutes after the fire broke out, while the first emergency response arrived 15 minutes later, the meeting was told.

The meeting was also informed that a fire had broken out at the Pims nursing hostel in July, a month before the incident, but no serious safety measures were taken at the hospital afterwards.

The ward had neither a fire alarm nor a sprinkler system, while the neonatal ward was found to be in violation of all relevant World Health Organisation (WHO) rules, according to the briefing.

There was also no officer specifically responsible for dealing with fires or other emergencies at the hospital. An assistant director had been assigned the additional responsibility, the meeting was told.

The meeting was further briefed on the hospital’s dilapidated condition and mismanagement. The prime minister thanked inquiry committee head Shahid Khan and its members and directed them to complete the investigation and submit a detailed report.

Federal ministers Ahsan Khan Cheema, Attaullah Tarar and Syed Mustafa Kamal, inquiry committee head Shahid Khan, members Barrister Nabeel Awan and Major General (retd) Khursheed Utra, and relevant senior officials attended the meeting.

Rs1m for nurse who saved child

PM Shehbaz also approved the Sitara-i-Khidmat award and a Rs1 million cash reward for nurse Razia Noreen, who “saved a child without regard for her own life”, the PMO said. Hospital officials said 15 newborns were in the ward when the fire broke out, one of whom was rescued.

The premier paid tribute to the nurse, praising her for saving the child “a few moments before the fire caused destruction”.

“Razia Noreen has demonstrated an exceptional sense of responsibility and humanity. The entire nation, including myself, is proud of Nurse Razia Noreen for risking her own life to save the child. Such dutiful individuals cannot be praised enough,” he was quoted as saying.

Ministers visit Pims

Earlier in the day, Health Minister Mustafa Kamal and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry visited the children’s ward at Pims.

Speaking to the media, he expressed the hope that findings of the inquiry committee would help clarify the circumstances surrounding the fire.

During the visit, the ministers met the families who lost their children in the tragedy. Kamal and Chaudhry conveyed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s condolences and sympathies to the bereaved families, while also expressing their own heartfelt condolences and deep sorrow over the loss.

“This is an extremely tragic and heartbreaking incident that cannot be adequately expressed in words,” Kamal said.

“We have come to share the pain and grief of the affected mothers and stand by them in this difficult time,” he said.

“The pain of a mother losing her child is a tragedy beyond words. There is no substitute for precious human lives, and the children who lost their lives cannot be brought back,” Kamal added.

He said the government and the entire nation stood with the affected families and shared their grief during the difficult time.

During their visit to Pims, the ministers reviewed the facilities and arrangements at the children’s ward and received a briefing from the hospital administration on the healthcare services being provided to patients.

Kamal said the government was awaiting the report of the inquiry committee constituted by PM Shehbaz to determine responsibility for the deadly fire.

“Let us wait for the report of the prime minister’s inquiry committee,” he said, adding that its findings would help clarify the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The ministers also reviewed the overall situation at the hospital and discussed measures to improve patient care and hospital management.

Later, they visited an affected family at their home in Rawalpindi, where Kamal presented cheques worth Rs5 million to the two families on behalf of the government.

“This financial assistance can in no way compensate for their loss,” he said, adding that it was only a gesture by the government to stand by the families and share in their responsibility.

Kamal said a complete and impartial investigation into the incident was under way.

“Strict action will be taken against those found responsible for this tragic incident,” he added.

‘There is only one committee’

Kamal, speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’ on Friday, rejected reports that three inquiry committees had been formed to investigate the fire at Pims, saying that only the panel constituted by the prime minister would probe the incident.

“There is only one committee formed by PM Shehbaz,” he said.

He said Shahid Khan was heading the committee investigating the incident. “It has been 24 hours; another 24 hours are left. They have to submit their report by tomorrow evening,” he said.

“Whatever its recommendations are, they must be implemented. Other than that, the entire exercise is useless,” he said.

“We will leave no stone unturned in implementing this committee’s recommendations and orders — whether an ED is named or anyone else,” he added.

Asked whether he had submitted his handwritten resignation to PM Shehbaz and whether the premier had refused to accept it, Kamal replied: “If you know this much, why are you asking me?”

Deadly fire at Pims

On Wednesday, 14 babies were killed after a fire erupted at the Mother and Child Healthcare Centre at Pims.

According to a Pims statement, the incident was “initially caused by a spark inside the nursery at 06:38am”, and within seconds a massive fire erupted due to oxygen points at each incubator. It said two doctors and two nurses on duty responded immediately and called security staff, who tried twice to enter the nursery before a blast occurred and the ceilings collapsed.

But, witnesses said they waited hours for emergency services and were forced to smash windows to reach the affected ward, while some alleged that doors were locked.

The hospital and government later disputed claims of delays and locked emergency exits.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif formed a high-level inquiry committee to probe the incident and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri.

Speaking in the Senate on Friday, Kamal said the tragedy could not become an “episode lasting merely a few days” and backed a parliamentary probe into the incident. He called for a wider investigation, saying it would expose a larger “rot” in the health sector.

Calling the health system “rotten”, Kamal said the Pims deaths should become a basis for reforms to prevent similar tragedies. Responding to calls for his resignation, he said, “Let the investigation be completed. I have already taken action beyond what they are thinking.”

The Senate unanimously passed a resolution seeking a special committee to investigate the fire, while the National Assembly also called for an impartial inquiry and strict action over negligence or safety lapses. The government has announced Rs5 million compensation for each affected family.

The tragedy has since sparked widespread outrage and calls for accountability, with the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on National Health Services also demanding answers from the Pims administration over possible negligence and safety lapses.

World.title: War weighs on Iran's economy as US intensifies sanctions
World.content:
Iranian leaders are acknowledging the economic toll of war with the US, with the supreme leader urging the government to address the hardship and the president saying foreign trade has shrunk by a third due to the American sanctions and blockade.

Yet Tehran signalled no retreat on Saturday, vowing to withstand US pressure, pursue diplomacy and maintain what it said was control over the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway giving Iran leverage through its ability to disrupt global energy markets.

The government said in a statement on state media that addressing economic pressures caused by sanctions and war was a central focus, including curbing inflation, managing markets, creating jobs, directing investment towards domestic production and gradually reducing dependence on the dollar.

Six months after the US and Israel launched the war, negotiations are at an impasse and President Donald Trump’s administration has stepped up efforts to punish Iran financially with what it has billed as an “economic D-Day”.

Sanctions compund toll on Iran’s economy

Washington has warned countries to cut business ties with Iran or face secondary sanctions, though the Treasury Department stopped short of imposing penalties against major Iranian trade partners such as China and India, which could have repercussions for the US and global economies.

The Treasury imposed sanctions on Egypt’s Banque Misr for doing business with Tehran, proposing a rule that would cut off the bank’s branches in the United Arab Emirates from dollar transactions.

Egypt’s central bank said it and the foreign ministry were in contact with US officials concerning the matter, adding the measure was limited to Banque Misr UAEs US dollar transactions with correspondent banks only.

Banque Misr said later in a statement it was reviewing the US Treasury notice, adding that its branch in the UAE continued to provide banking services to its customers in line with applicable rules and procedures.

The US also issued sanctions targeting an entity based in Hong Kong and a person linked to Iran’s Bank Melli, according to a notice on the Treasury website.

The sanctions drive compounds the toll of the war on Iran’s economy, where annual inflation hit 66 per cent last month.

Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei who has not been seen publicly since initial February 28 attack that assassinated his father and former supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, called on the government to tackle the economic hardship.

“There is the need to seriously address the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services,” according to a written statement attributed to Khamenei.

President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that Iranian exports and imports had slumped nearly 35pc because of US sanctions and a naval blockade of Iranian ports.

But he said Iran was able to sell about 90 million barrels of oil during the short-lived memorandum of understanding that the US and Iran signed in June, when Washington permitted Iranian oil sales.

Iran vows to pursue diplomacy and defence

With the US focused on its economic pressure campaign, others have sought to revive diplomatic efforts to end the war.

Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met with Iranian leaders in Tehran on Thursday. He said he had stressed during the meeting the importance of returning to the pre-war status of open shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi on Friday described the talks with Al Thani as “creative”.

In Saturday’s statement, Iran said diplomacy and defence were “two complementary, coordinated and inseparable wings” for protecting the country’s national interests, security and territorial integrity. It said it would pursue both tracks in a balanced manner.

Qatar, a US ally and Gulf neighbour to Iran, and Pakistan helped broker the Islamabad memorandum of understanding that led to a brief ceasefire before disagreements over the vital strait caused it to unravel. Before the war, the waterway carried 20pc of the world’s oil and LNG.

US military commanders claim American forces have cleared sea mines from the strait that had been laid months ago by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

Trump has repeatedly said the Strait of Hormuz is open, but the Revolutionary Guards’ navy said in a statement that such claims “are an obvious lie”, reiterating that the waterway remained closed to ships without Iranian permission.

Only seven commodity vessels transited the strait on Thursday, down from 17 a day earlier and below the 10-day average of 15, preliminary shipping data showed on Friday.

World.title: Govt apologises for ‘temporary’ night-time loadshedding due to unavailability of RLNG
World.content:
The government on Saturday apologised to consumers for electricity loadshedding during the night, attributing it to the unavailability of regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG), and assured them that load management would be reduced “as soon as” the delayed RLNG cargoes arrived.

In a statement, the Power Division spokesperson said temporary load management of 1.5 to three hours had been carried out during last night’s peak hours due to a 3,600MW shortfall resulting from the unavailability of RLNG after a cargo failed to arrive on time. The situation was compounded by a 195MW decline in generation from Mangla Dam.

Furnace oil-based power plants were also brought into operation during peak hours so that the electricity demand in the country could be met during the night hours, the statement added.

“This temporary load management will be reduced as soon as the RLNG cargoes arrive,” it stated.

The Power Division stressed that consumers needed to “moderate their electricity usage during peak hours at night so that load management can be kept to a minimum”.

“There is no load management during the day. However, in areas where load management is carried out due to losses, electricity is being supplied as per the schedule,” it added.

The statement concluded with an apology for the “temporary load management during night hours due to the unavailability of RLNG”.

The government had also apologised to power consumers in April for loadshedding exceeding the promised 2.25 hours, arising out of lower water availability for power generation.

The US-Iran war, which began on February 28, has disrupted the supply of RLNG cargoes from Qatar via the Strait of Hormuz. This resulted in the government purchasing five expensive cargoes from the spot market in July, with the sale price of RLNG witnessing the biggest-ever increase in the commodity’s decade-long history.

Consequently, the cost of RLNG-based power generation surged by a record 242 per cent to Rs47.4 per unit in July, from less than Rs14 in April.

Chiefly because of the LNG factor, the power companies have sought a Rs2.52 per unit increase in fuel cost adjustment (FCA) to consumers across the country in September bills despite 73pc generation in July from cheaper domestic, predominantly zero-cost fuel sources. LNG contributed about 11pc of the total grid supply.

World.title: Rescuers claw through mud as Nepal, China flood death toll climbs to 675
World.content:
Devastating floods near Nepal’s border with China this week have killed at least 675 people in Nepal, the Himalayan nation’s disaster authority said on Saturday.

Chinese state media earlier confirmed seven dead in Tibet following Wednesday’s disaster, taking the total killed to 682.

Rescuers in both countries were battling to locate thousands of people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan region, engulfing entire villages.

The number of missing in Nepal remained constant at 2,426, after a sharp hike in numbers on Saturday morning. That missing list includes 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the river where the torrent smashed down, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

The number of missing also includes 45 Nepali Army soldiers, 40 police officers, and 19 immigration and customs officers.

In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims. However, they are not included in the toll.

Rescue worker Kawan Koirala, from the Nepal Scout Disaster Response Team, said they were struggling in thick, leg-sucking mud.

“People want their want their family’s body back, either dead or alive, but we cannot find them… you can see the mud,” he told AFP, exhausted after an 18 hour shift.

“It is very traumatic for me too. It is my first time seeing these types of things. Everywhere is mud. We faced floods in Nepal before, but not like this.”

A man takes pictures in front of damaged buildings after flash floods and a mudslide, in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 29, 2026. — Reuters

The US Geological Survey said the disaster on Wednesday on the Tibet-Nepal border was caused by a glacial collapse that created a torrent of debris downstream.

Those that made it out say they have lost everything and now face an agonising wait to discover the fate of missing loved ones, and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.

“All the settlements near the river were swept away. There is nothing left,” survivor Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP.

“There is nothing left.”

At Bidur’s army base, a key rescue hub in the same district, relatives crowded around lists of rescued people pasted on a wall.

Samjhana Thing said she had been waiting three days for news of her missing brother.

“We don’t know anything. Hopefully he is in a safe place,” she said.

“I have come here looking for my son,” said Kalka Sharda, scanning the list in desperation.

“He was a labourer at the hydropower plant, but I can’t find his name, and the authorities are not saying anything.”

A person holds an umbrella as he stands in front of damaged buildings after flash floods and a mudslide, in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 29, 2026. — Reuters

In an area home to vast energy infrastructure projects, Nepal’s disaster authority listed 933 hydropower workers among the missing, along with 517 foreigners, including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.

Risk of lake burst near disaster site wanes

The threat of a lake formed after the glacier collapse has eased, Chinese authorities said on Saturday, as it appears to have shrunk.

Satellite images from Thursday to Saturday morning suggest that water in the lake, which straddles the border between China’s Tibet region and Nepal at the confluence of two rivers, has been slowly flowing out and gradually reducing the reservoir, state broadcaster CCTV reported, citing the Water Resources Ministry.

By Saturday afternoon, parts of the lake bed had become visible, CCTV reported.

The ministry said satellite imagery of the lake on the Purepu Tsangpo river showed it covered 99,000 square metres early on Saturday, roughly the size of 14 soccer pitches, having shrunk by 21,000 square metres since Thursday.

‘Enormous’ trauma

The trauma of Wednesday’s catastrophe has been “enormous”, and as many as 93,000 people may have been affected, the Red Cross said, with the death toll expected to rise.

Emergency teams worked flat out to find survivors as widespread devastation left communities short of food and water.

Fears of further flooding have compounded the search for the missing.

The deluge of ice and mud caused huge lakes, and one of these formations has become a risk of further floods.

While the exact cause of the collapse is unclear, climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of such disasters.

Children displaced by flash floods and a mudslide rest inside a relief camp in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 29, 2026. — Reuters

In Tibet, where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, Beijing had paused its rescue operation at the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of renewed flooding.

On the Nepali side, soldiers were trying desperately to drill through to 100 people trapped in the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Saturday.

The prime minister’s office said teams had begun “clearing mud and debris” to open the entrance, while a specialised Indian tunnel rescue unit had arrived to help.

Nepal reported a death toll of 626 people on Saturday. There are 2,426 people, including hundreds of foreigners, who are out of contact in Nepal.

Across the border in Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, seven people died and 554 remain missing, the state Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.

Authorities also said they had evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet.

In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.

‘All swept away’

On the Nepali side of the border, the military located people trapped in the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project, where they were working to find a way in to extract the survivors.

“Two helicopters have been dispatched, but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel,” army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.

Rescuer load relief material in a helicopter to be transported to the areas affected by flash floods and a mudslide as it drizzles at the Maithali Barrack, an army training center, in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 29, 2026. — Reuters

Some 350 workers and residents have been brought to safety from the site, he added, but efforts were ongoing to rescue more than a hundred trapped in the same area.

Workers rescued from other dam projects along the Trishuli valley described a disaster that unfolded with terrifying speed.

Buddha Tamang told AFP he survived only because he was inside a tunnel at the dam where he worked when the flood struck.

“The senior officers working on the other side, they were all swept away,” Tamang, who was airlifted on Thursday after being marooned for more than 24 hours, told AFP.

Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among those missing on the border, as many were on a pilgrimage to Tibet’s Mount Kailash.

Sivaranjani Muthunathan was travelling by bus with 56 others towards the Chinese border when they became stuck in what they thought was a traffic jam.

“Then there was fog, smoke, something that seemed to suddenly engulf us,” Muthunathan, 46, told AFP on Friday, showing a phone video she recorded of a torrent surging towards her.

A man walks past a damaged house after the flash floods and mudslide, at Devighat, Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 29, 2026. — Reuters

Around them, vehicles were swept away or buried under mud.

“One by one, we also climbed out through the driver’s side,” then scrambled up a hill, she said.

World.title: Bangladesh confirms deal to buy Chinese J-10 fighter jets: report
World.content:
Bangladesh has confirmed a deal to purchase China’s 4.5-generation J-10CE fighter jets, citing the aircraft’s reported combat performance against French-made Rafale jets during the brief Pakistan-India conflict in May, the South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported on Friday.

The Chengdu J-10C is a single-engine, multirole combat aircraft manufactured in China. Boasting a top speed of Mach 1.8, it can be fitted with a variety of air-to-air and air-to-ground munitions. It played a key role on the first night of hostilities, shooting down six jets belonging to the Indian Air Force.

The Information and Broadcasting Adviser to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh Zahedur Rahman said earlier this week that a draft proposal to buy the jets had been submitted to the country’s finance ministry and Armed Forces Division for final approval, SCMP reported citing the Bangladeshi Press Information Department (PID).

According to the Bangladesh PID, the draft proposal also includes the purchase of Chinese attack helicopters, VIP transport helicopters and drones.

“Subject to necessary budgetary allocation in the current fiscal year, this procurement will be executed immediately; otherwise, it will roll over into the next budget cycle,” it added.

SCMP reports that Rahman said Bangladesh “paid attention” to the war last year, when Pakistan used J-10 fighters and PL-15 long-range air-to-air missiles to shoot down Indian Rafales.

In January this year, Pakistan and Bangladesh’s air chiefs held detailed discussions on the “potential procurement” of the locally-produced JF-17 Thunder aircraft, according to Inter-Services Public Relations.

It added that Bangladesh Air Force Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan called on Pakistan Air Force Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Babar Sidhu in Islamabad, where “The meeting focused on strengthening operational cooperation and institutional synergy, with emphasis on training, capacity building, and collaboration in aerospace advancements.”

A day later, Dhaka’s air chief discussed avenues for enhancing defence cooperation with Pakistan in separate meetings with Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf.

A year ago , Pakistan was engaged in a military conflict with India, dealing the boastful neighbour an internationally recognised “ clear setback ”.

The conflict with India, starting from the April 22 Pahalgam attack to the end of Operation Bunyanum Marsoos, with a ceasefire ending a military escalation between the two countries on May 10, has been called “ Marka-i-Haq ” (Battle of Truth) by the state.

But from the night of May 6 to May 10, the drums of war were echoing loudly across South Asia as the nuclear-armed arch-rivals exchanged missiles, raising global alarm over the risk of unpredictable escalation.

World.title: Inquiry ordered as CCTV footage emerges of police's alleged involvement in scuffle in Karachi's DHA
World.content:
